items.body: On this episode of On the Midwatch, Lessons in Sea Stories, Submariners talk about their life on submarines above the Arctic Circle and their participation in the U.S. Navy’s Ice Exercise or ICEX. Operation Ice Camp (OIC), formally known as ICEX, is a United States Navy biennial mission in the Arctic Ocean that establishes a temporary camp on floating sea ice. It is designed to complete arctic warfare objectives both operations and strategic as identified by in DoD, NAVY, and Submarine Force directives. The US Navy employs submarines from the Atlantic and Pacific Fleets. When available, allied submarines may participate. In addition to several US Navy Commands, the Marine Corps, Air National Guard, and Army National Guard have participated extensively along with international military from the United Kingdom, Canada, France, and Australia. Additionally, the scientific community and universities participate in research and development supported by the US Navy Ice Camp. Hosted by STSC Antonio Maldonado, filmed by Brian Powell, and produced by Lauren Belknap. Guests are Capt. Matthew Fanning, CMC Mike Micheli, and YNS1 Taylor Gilbert.
items.summaryZh: 在《On the Midwatch，海上故事课》的这一期节目中，潜艇兵们讲述了他们在北极圈以北的潜艇上的生活经历，以及他们参与美国海军“冰上演习”（ICEX）的情况。该演习的正式名称为“冰上营地行动”（OIC），是美国海军每两年在北冰洋开展的一次行动，会在浮动的海冰上搭建临时营地，其目的便是实现美国国防部、海军及潜艇部队所制定的各项作战与战略目标。
items.titleZh: 《On the Midwatch，海上故事课》：冰上演习背后的故事
zhParas: 在《On the Midwatch，海上故事课》的这一期节目中，潜艇兵们讲述了他们在北极圈以北的潜艇上的生活经历，以及他们参与美国海军“冰上演习”（ICEX）的情况。该演习正式名称为“冰上营地行动”（OIC），是美国海军每两年在北冰洋开展的一次行动，会在浮动的海冰上搭建临时营地。其目的是实现美国国防部、海军及潜艇部队所制定的各项作战与战略目标。参与此次演习的美国海军潜艇来自大西洋舰队和太平洋舰队，如有条件的话，盟国潜艇也会加入。除了多个美国海军司令部外，海军陆战队、空军国民自卫队和陆军国民自卫队也深度参与了演习，同时还有来自英国、加拿大、法国和澳大利亚的国际军队参与。此外，科学界和各大学也在美国海军冰上营地的支持下从事相关研究工作。本期节目由STSC的安东尼奥·马尔多纳多主持，布赖恩·鲍威尔负责拍摄，劳伦·贝尔克纳普负责制作，嘉宾包括马修·范宁上校、迈克·米凯利海军指挥官以及泰勒·吉尔伯特海军下士。

items.title: No need to be grebe – federal agencies share water between birds and other obligations
items.author: Tom Conning
items.summary: Western and Clark’s grebes (pronounced “greeb,” so forgive the attempted wordplay) have specific needs for nesting and the pool behind McNary Lock and Dam near the Tri-Cities in Washington state can be a good spot. If water levels don’t fluctuate too much, mats of vegetation can grow, which entice the birds to nest on them. However, the pool has a narrow elevation range to support nesting – high water levels can dislodge the floating vegetation mats and wash the nests away.
items.body: Western and Clark’s grebes (pronounced “greeb,” so forgive the attempted wordplay) have specific needs for nesting and the pool behind McNary Lock and Dam near the Tri-Cities in Washington state can be a good spot. If water levels don’t fluctuate too much, mats of vegetation can grow, which entice the birds to nest on them. However, the pool has a narrow elevation range to support nesting – high water levels can dislodge the floating vegetation mats and wash the nests away. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) doesn’t monitor grebe activities at McNary Dam, as that isn’t part of its normal operations, but the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) does at McNary National Wildlife Refuge, just downstream. USACE and USFWS are close partners and have been working together to implement operations to support the birds. The agencies tried a similar operation last year but local conditions disrupted the grebes’ nesting plans. The agencies made another attempt this year. “The McNary National Wildlife Refuge asked us to lower the reservoir elevation and minimize water level fluctuations in the McNary pool for about a month to help support grebe nesting,” said Aaron Marshall, Northwestern Division Reservoir Control Center chief. “The request fits within our normal operating range, allowing us to support the request,” he said. “Our goal is to balance this request with other operational objectives at McNary Dam. It also shows that adaptive management of the system, within our normal operating ranges, can have multiple benefits.” Rare in this part of Washington, grebes are candidates for listing by the Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife and are a Bird of Conservation Concern for the Great Basin Conservation Region. Twelve of the 14 states where these birds nest have identified them as species of greatest conservation need in their State Wildlife Action plans. “We were ecstatic to discover these birds nesting at McNary National Wildlife Refuge,” said Steve Kahl, refuge manager. “It’s a great opportunity for our agencies to collaborate toward conserving two species that have very specific habitat requirements in order to nest successfully,” he said. USFWS made the 2026 request on July 14, and USACE staff found it was an operation the Reservoir Control Center (RCC) at Northwestern Division could support. Natural conditions such as wind and streamflows, alongside sometimes competing operational objectives like navigation safety and hydropower affect the success of this operation. “There are so many demands for how we manage water throughout the Columbia River Basin, sometimes we have to make difficult decisions,” said Leah Hamilton, Northwestern Division water regulator. “Fortunately, we were able to work with Bonneville Power Administration to find an operation that could work for the grebes and balance other demands on the system,” she said. “We look forward to working with U.S. Fish and Wildlife, and BPA to refine operations to better help the grebes reproduce.” To date, USFWS observers counted 26 young grebes and 18 nests in the area.
items.summaryZh: 西氏鸊鷉和克拉克鸊鷉在筑巢方面有特定的需求，而华盛顿州三城附近麦克纳里水闸和大坝后的水池正是理想的筑巢地点。如果水位波动不大，水中的水生植被会逐渐生长，吸引这些鸟类在上面筑巢。不过，该水池的适宜筑巢海拔范围很窄——水位过高时，漂浮的水生植被会被冲走，导致鸟巢也被冲毁。

items.title: MSCPAC Employee Shares Name with Newest Expeditionary Fast Transport Ship USNS Cody
items.author: Sarah Cannon
items.summary: Samuel Cody, assistant security manager and security officer for Military Sealift Command Pacific, and his family visited the Military Sealift Command (MSC) expeditionary fast transport ship USNS Cody (T-EPF 14) while it was in port in San Diego.
items.body: San Diego, Calif.-Samuel Cody, assistant security manager and security officer for Military Sealift Command Pacific, and his family visited the Military Sealift Command (MSC) expeditionary fast transport ship USNS Cody (T-EPF 14) while it was in port in San Diego. Cody is a fifth-generation descendant of William Frederick Cody, better known as Buffalo Bill Cody. The city of Cody, Wyoming — the ship’s namesake — was named for Buffalo Bill Cody. Cody; his mother, Wanda; and his 11-year-old son, Daniel, received a tour from Capt. Chris Jackson, the ship’s civil service master. They learned about the ship’s mission and damage-control procedures, and reviewed its lifeboats, rafts, rigid-hull inflatable boat launching systems and medical facilities. “It was really great to be able to take my family aboard a ship that has the same name as us,” Cody said. “Seeing our family name on the ship gave me a sense of familial pride. “It meant a lot to have my son see this ship. He wants to be an aerospace engineer and loved learning about the jet propulsion system aboard.” USNS Cody is the 14th EPF in the MSC sealift program. The all-aluminum catamarans provide high-speed, shallow-draft transportation and are designed to rapidly move medium-sized cargo for the Navy, Marine Corps and Army. The ships can support a range of military and civilian contingencies, including noncombatant evacuation operations and humanitarian assistance. The ship is the second variant of the EPF or a Flight II. Flight II ships have an enhanced medical mission capability, with an embarked medical unit, two operating rooms, and the ability to support approximately 41 medical patients, and 147 embarked forces. In addition, Flight II EPFs have an 11-meter Rigid Inflatable Boat (RIB) for special operations use, and flight deck that can accommodate the MV-22 Osprey aircraft. USNS Cody will spend several weeks in San Diego before transiting to the U.S. 7th Fleet area of operations for future tasking.
items.summaryZh: 加利福尼亚州圣地亚哥——美军太平洋海运司令部的安保副主管兼安保官员塞缪尔·科迪携家人，参观了停靠在圣地亚哥港的海军海运司令部远征快速运输舰USNS科迪号（T-EPF 14）。科迪是更为人熟知的“水牛比尔·科迪”威廉·弗雷德里克·科迪的第五代后裔，而这艘舰艇的命名来源——怀俄明州的科迪市，也正是以水牛比尔·科迪的名字命名的。在舰艇的文职主管克里斯·杰克逊上尉的带领下，科迪、他的母亲旺达以及11岁的儿子丹尼尔参观了舰艇，了解了其执行任务的相关流程及灾难应对措施，还查看了舰上的救生艇、救生筏、硬壳充气艇发射系统以及医疗设施。科迪表示：“能带家人登上与我们同名的舰艇真是太棒了，看到舰艇上印着我们的姓氏，让我感受到了家族的荣耀。让儿子看到这艘舰艇对他意义重大，他立志成为一名航空航天工程师，还非常感兴趣地了解了舰上的喷气推进系统。”USNS科迪号是海军海运司令部远征快速运输舰系列中的第14艘舰艇。这类全铝制双体船具备高速航行和低吃水深度的特点，专为快速为海军、海军陆战队和陆军运送中型货物而设计，可应对各类军事及民用紧急情况，包括非战斗人员撤离行动和人道主义援助任务。该舰属于远征快速运输舰的第二代型号，即Flight II型，其医疗能力更为强大，配备有舰载医疗单元、两间手术室，可同时为约41名患者提供治疗，并为147名舰载人员提供支援。此外，Flight II型远征快速运输舰还配备有一艘11米长的硬壳充气艇用于执行特殊任务，其飞行甲板可容纳MV-22鱼鹰直升机。USNS科迪号将在圣地亚哥停留数周，之后将前往美国第七舰队责任区执行后续任务。

items.title: Rubio says US, Greece to jointly combat security threats
items.author: Ivana Sekularac, Angeliki Koutantou, Lefteris Papadimas, Jonathan Landay, Reuters
items.summary: The U.S. and Greece are launching a joint security program to strengthen counterterrorism information sharing between their law enforcement agencies.
items.body:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Wednesday that “strong and model NATO ally” Greece and the United States are launching new counterterrorism information sharing between their law enforcement agencies.

During an official visit to Athens, Rubio said Greece was particularly exposed to the threats posed by mass migration and human trafficking.

“As part of our efforts to combat these common threats to our nations, we’re proud to announce a new memorandum of understanding establishing a joint security program to strengthen the counterterrorism information sharing between our respective law enforcement agencies,” he told reporters alongside Greek Foreign Minister George Gerapetritis.

Greece has been an important NATO ally to the United States, offering key military facilities to safeguard security in the Eastern Mediterranean, and it leads an EU maritime mission to protect commercial shipping in the Red Sea.

Rubio and Gerapetritis presided over the sixth round of a U.S.-Greece strategic dialogue that began in 2018 in which the sides agreed “to deepen defense ties, bolster trade and investment, and promote cultural ties,” according to a joint statement.

Greece, it said, would receive $4 billion to support a long-term defense plan to increase interoperability between the two militaries and to “explore future opportunities for defense industrial base cooperation.”

Gerapetritis said that Greece was willing to cooperate with the United States and offer maritime aid in the Strait of Hormuz if there is a viable peace process there.

Rubio stood by U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle after U.S. senators expressed concerns over allegations that she had threatened that the U.S. could use its influence to undermine the Greek government.

Asked if her conduct was in compliance with State Department ethics, Rubio said: “Suffice it to say, our embassy here is doing a great job. Our ambassador has been a strong ambassador here.”
items.summaryZh: 美国与希腊正在推出一项联合安全计划，旨在加强两国执法机构之间的反恐信息共享机制。
items.titleZh: 卢比奥称美希将携手应对安全威胁
zhParas: 美国国务卿马可·卢比奥周三表示，作为‘强大且堪称典范的北约盟友’的希腊与美国正在推动两国执法机构之间开展新的反恐信息共享机制。
在雅典的正式访问期间，卢比奥表示，希腊尤其面临大规模移民和人口贩卖所带来的安全威胁。
在与希腊外交部长乔治·格拉佩特里蒂斯一同接受记者采访时，卢比奥表示：‘为共同应对这些威胁两国安全的共同挑战，我们很高兴宣布达成一项新的谅解备忘录，旨在建立一项联合安全计划，从而加强两国执法机构在反恐信息共享方面的合作。’
作为美国重要的北约盟友，希腊不仅提供关键的军事设施以维护东地中海地区的安全，还牵头开展欧盟海上任务，旨在保护红海地区的商业航运安全。
根据双方发布的联合声明，鲁比奥与格拉佩特里蒂斯共同主持了始于2018年的第六轮美希战略对话。在会谈中，双方同意“深化防务合作，加强贸易与投资往来，并促进文化交流”。
据称，希腊将获得40亿美元资金，用于支持一项长期国防计划，旨在提升两国军队的协同作战能力，并“探索国防工业领域未来的合作机遇”。
格拉佩特里蒂斯表示，如果霍尔木兹海峡能够启动可行的和平进程，希腊愿与美国携手合作，并为该地区的安全保障提供海上援助。
在多名美国参议员对金伯利·吉尔福伊尔涉嫌威胁称美国会利用自身影响力削弱希腊政府表示担忧后，鲁比奥站出来为这位美国驻希腊大使辩护。
当被问及她的行为是否符合美国国务院的道德规范时，鲁比奥回应称：‘可以说，我们在这里的大使馆工作表现极为出色，我们的大使也是一位非常出色的驻希腊大使。’

items.title: Strategic Industry Partnerships Secure V-22 Osprey Operational Readiness and Supply Chain Agility Beyond 2055
items.author: Neil Lobeda
items.summary: Global supply chain optimization and advanced sustainment strategies for the V-22 Osprey platform took center stage at a recent Team Osprey Working Group. A coalition of 200 defense experts representing six allied nations and seven U.S. government agencies integrated efforts to secure tilt-rotor fleet readiness beyond 2055.
items.body:
Global supply chain optimization and advanced sustainment strategies for the V-22 Osprey platform took center stage at a recent Team Osprey Working Group. A coalition of 200 defense experts representing six allied nations and seven U.S. government agencies integrated efforts to secure tilt-rotor fleet readiness beyond 2055. Driven by Bell Boeing and PMA-275, the V-22 Joint Program Office, this collaborative network of over 35 premier defense, engineering, and manufacturing suppliers focused on generating immediate material availability and expanding technical modernization.

Expanding the industrial base to counter near-peer threats, the initiative recently injected fresh technical expertise into the sustainment ecosystem by integrating 14 first-time industry participants. By accelerating component reliability and optimizing supply chain modifications, this unified coalition ensures the V-22 continues to serve as a force multiplier, delivering unmatched versatility, speed, and range across multiple operational domains.

"Synchronizing our global supply chain and integrating technical innovations directly translates to higher material availability on the flight line," said Col Robert Hurst, PMA-275 program manager. "Optimizing component reliability across our defense industry partners ensures deployed commanders maintain the rapid expeditionary lift and logistical flexibility required to operate effectively in high-threat environments."

Targeted improvements across the V-22 enterprise directly sustain critical operational roles the platform executes for the Joint Force. For the U.S. Marine Corps, securing the core tactical medium-lift platform ensures rapid troop movement and critical assault support remain a decisive advantage for expeditionary force projection worldwide. Furthermore, fortifying the Carrier Onboard Delivery (COD) mission guarantees seamless supply flow, passenger transfer, and critical high-value maritime logistics to U.S. Navy carrier strike groups deployed across global maritime theaters. Finally, advancing long-range infiltration, exfiltration, and resupply capabilities provides U.S. Special Operations Command (SOCOM) and Air Force Special Operations Command (AFSOC) with unparalleled special operations reach and mobility into contested and remote environments.

The continued alignment of research, sustainment, and fleet support resources solidifies the V-22 Osprey's technological superiority, ensuring the tilt-rotor fleet remains fully capable of meeting evolving global threats and delivering a warfighting advantage to the Nation for decades to come.

About PMA-275 PMA-275 is the V-22 Joint Program Office responsible for the lifecycle management, procurement, development, and sustainment of the V-22 Osprey tilt-rotor aircraft variants across the U.S. Marine Corps, U.S. Navy, U.S. Air Force Special Operations Command, and our international partner.

为应对日益严峻的同等实力对手威胁，该计划通过引入14家首次参与该项目的企业，为V-22“鱼鹰”飞行器的维护保障体系注入了新的技术力量。凭借提升零部件可靠性及优化供应链管理的举措，这一由多方组成的联合体确保了该倾转旋翼机能够在未来持续发挥其作战优势，为各类作战任务提供无与伦比的灵活性、速度及作战范围。
PMA-275项目负责人罗伯特·赫斯特上校表示：“通过优化全球供应链并引入各类技术创新，能够直接提升飞行任务中所需物资的供应效率。”他进一步指出：“通过提升各国防工业合作伙伴的零部件可靠性，可确保驻扎在一线的指挥官们始终拥有强大的快速投送能力与灵活的物流保障体系，从而在威胁极高的作战环境中高效执行任务。

对V-22“鱼鹰”飞行平台整体体系进行的针对性改进，直接保障了该平台为联合部队执行各项关键作战任务的能力。对于美国海军陆战队而言，确保这一核心战术中型运输平台始终处于良好战备状态，意味着部队能够实现快速机动，并在世界各地的远征行动中提供关键的攻击支援，从而保持其作为远征力量优势的地位。此外，强化航母舰载补给功能能够为部署在全球各海洋战区的美国海军航母打击群提供顺畅的物资补给、人员转运以及高价值的海运物流保障。最后，提升远程渗透、撤离和补给能力，使得美国特种作战司令部与空军特种作战司令部能够在充满挑战的偏远环境中拥有无与伦比的特种作战覆盖范围与机动性。
通过持续整合研发、维护及舰队支援资源，V-22“鱼鹰”飞行平台的技术优势得以进一步巩固，这确保了这类倾转旋翼机队始终具备应对日益复杂的全球安全威胁的能力，从而在未来数十年里为美国军队带来显著的作战优势。
PMA-275即为V-22联合项目办公室，负责全美海军陆战队、美国海军、美国空军特种作战司令部以及各国际合作伙伴所使用的各类V-22“鱼鹰”倾转旋翼机型的全生命周期管理、采购、研发及后续维护工作。

items.title: Air University captures lessons from Air Force ACE implementation
items.author: Billy Blankenship
items.summary: After helping lead the Air Force's implementation of Agile Combat Employment, Sandeep Mulgund wanted to document what the service learned while moving ACE from an emerging concept into the way the Air Force operates.
items.body:
MAXWELL AIR FORCE BASE, Ala. -- After helping lead the Air Force's implementation of Agile Combat Employment, Sandeep Mulgund wanted to document what the service learned while moving ACE from an emerging concept into the way the Air Force operates.

He didn't want to do it right away.

Mulgund left the Air Staff in April 2025, after the work wrapped up at the end of 2024. He wanted some distance from the effort before looking back at what happened and what might help the next team asked to take on something similar.

“I was less interested in those kinds of tactical sort of immediate reactions and more interested in looking back on it with the passage of time and putting things in context to be able to have a bit broader perspective,” Mulgund said during an Air University Press Author Connect interview.

The idea eventually came to Air University.

Mulgund pitched it to then-Air University commander Lt. Gen. Andrea Tullos in September 2025. Air University captured the resulting work through Air University Press in Implementing New Airpower Concepts: Insights from Agile Combat Employment .

Mulgund wasn't trying to write only about ACE. He also wanted to capture lessons that could help the next team trying to move a major effort across the Air Force.

“There’s always the next initiative to get after as our idea for operations, the threat environment, and new technologies evolve,” Mulgund said. “I thought there were some things we learned that the next such team can use to enable them to accelerate whatever they’re getting after.”

“A large part of it was just learning how to coordinate a big endeavor across the entire Air Force,” he said.

Some of those lessons came from looking much further back.

For decades, the Air Force had grown accustomed to generating airpower from large, fixed locations in largely uncontested environments. Mulgund found examples from an earlier era when that wasn't the case.

He looked to the 8th Air Force operating from England, the 9th Air Force on the European continent, Gen. Douglas MacArthur's island-hopping campaign in the South Pacific and the Flying Tigers in China during World War II.

Those forces also had to figure out how to generate airpower while operating under threat.

“What we have done with ACE over the last few years is part of a larger evolution of air power,” Mulgund said.

Mulgund also looked at how the Air Force organized the ACE effort.

The service established an ACE working group that operated much like an operations planning team. People from across the Air Force joined the effort, many while still doing their regular jobs.

The working group wasn't supposed to become permanent.

“Once you get to some kind of steady state, it is time to fold the work back into normal staff processes rather than it being a special initiative,” Mulgund said.

By fall 2024, he believed ACE had reached that point. The concept had been embedded in Air Force doctrine, appropriations and technology development.

“Disbanding the working group was the right decision,” Mulgund said.

There was still work left to do.

“I would say that the area where the most work remains to be done is joint integration,” Mulgund said.

The Army has multidomain operations. The Marine Corps has expeditionary advanced base operations. The Navy has distributed maritime operations. Each service has worked through its own approach to operating with a lighter footprint and generating combat power across domains.

Mulgund said the services then have to figure out how those approaches work together.

“What often tends to happen is that each military service first works to figure out what they are doing, and then they figure out how to make it work across the joint force,” he said.

Joint exercises are part of that process.

“The services don’t really start to figure it out until they conduct joint exercises like Bamboo Eagle,” Mulgund said. “So, there remains a fair bit of work to do in terms of military service crosspollination as we move forward.”

The Air Force has also worked through ACE with allies and partners.

Mulgund pointed to the Royal Air Force and Royal Australian Air Force, along with the Royal Canadian Air Force, French Air and Space Force and Korean Air Force, as partners working through similar questions about generating airpower from different locations and under different conditions.

His work on ACE has also led him toward another subject.

Mulgund is developing a book on command and control. He said discussions about command and control often focus on technology, communications systems and resilient networks.

Those things matter, he said, but they aren't enough on their own.

“Indeed, these aspects of command and control are critical,” Mulgund said. “However, they cannot take command and control forward on their own.”

For Mulgund, it comes back to people making decisions when they don't have perfect information.

“What is required is that we get back to the fundamentals of command and control, or what I call the human endeavor of decision making in the presence of uncertainty,” he said.

Technology will keep changing. So will the operating environment. Mulgund said uncertainty will remain.

“Uncertainty and complexity, fog and friction, have never gone away,” Mulgund said. “They just evolve and transform.”

That's part of why Mulgund wanted some distance before looking back at ACE.

The next Air Force-wide effort won't look exactly like this one. Mulgund's point was that the people working it shouldn't have to relearn everything his team learned while moving ACE across the service.

That's where the work fits at Air University.

Mulgund brought experience from an Air Force-wide operational change effort into the university. Air University Press provided the publishing capability to capture those lessons and make them available to the force.

It's one example of Air University operating as an integrated enterprise. The university brings together capabilities from across its schools, centers and other organizations based on what a problem requires. In this case, publishing helped preserve lessons from an operational effort. Other problems may call for education, research, doctrine, wargaming or technical expertise.

That approach supports Air University's work to forge expert joint warfighters and solve operational problems for the Joint Force.

Mulgund's paper also leaves some questions open. He identifies joint integration as an area where more work remains and is carrying lessons from ACE into his research on command and control, where his focus is on people making decisions under uncertainty.

For him, the reason for writing the paper was simpler.

“There’s always the next initiative to get after,” he said.

He wanted the people working that next initiative to have the lessons from this one.
items.summaryZh: 在协助领导空军推进‘敏捷作战运用’计划的实施之后，桑迪普·穆尔贡德希望将空军在将这一新兴概念转化为实际作战模式的过程中所积累的经验教训记录下来。
items.titleZh: 空军大学总结空军“敏捷作战运用”计划实施中的经验教训
zhParas: 阿拉巴马州马克斯韦尔空军基地——在协助领导空军推进“敏捷作战运用”计划的实施之后，桑迪普·穆尔贡德希望将空军在将这一新兴概念转化为实际作战模式的过程中所积累的经验教训记录下来。
他并不想立刻着手进行这项工作。
2024年底相关工作结束后，穆尔冈德于2025年4月离开了空军参谋部。在回顾过往经验以及总结哪些经验能为后续承担类似任务的团队提供帮助之前，他希望先与这项工作保持一定距离。
穆尔冈德在空军大学出版社举办的作者交流活动中表示：“我并不太关注那些即时的战术反应，反而更希望随着时间推移回顾整个过程，将各项举措置于更宏观的背景中加以分析，从而获得更广阔的视野。
这一想法最终传到了空军大学。
2025年9月，穆尔贡德将这一想法向当时的空军大学司令安德里亚·图洛斯中将提出。空军大学通过其出版社出版了《实施新型空中力量概念：敏捷作战运用带来的启示》一书，对相关研究成果进行了整理记录。
穆尔贡德的目的并非仅记录有关“敏捷作战运用”这一概念的内容，他还想总结出那些经验教训，以便为后续试图在空军内部推广类似重大变革的团队提供参考。
穆尔贡德表示：“随着我们的作战理念、威胁环境以及新技术的不断演变，总会有新的任务需要去完成。我认为我们在推动‘敏捷作战运用’这一举措的过程中积累了一些经验，这些经验可供后续负责类似变革的团队借鉴，从而更快地推进他们手头的各项工作。
他说：“其中很大一部分工作就是学习如何协调整个空军范围内的大规模行动。
其中一些经验教训源自对更久远历史的回顾。
数十年来，空军一直习惯在几乎没有竞争的环境中，从大型固定基地出发来部署空中力量。但穆尔冈德找到了早期并非如此的实例作为对照。
他以驻扎在英格兰的第八空军、位于欧洲大陆的第九空军、道格拉斯·麦克阿瑟将军在南太平洋发动的岛链进攻行动，以及二战期间在中国作战的飞虎队作为参考案例。
这些部队还必须在面临威胁的作战环境下设法构建空中作战力量。
过去几年里我们通过ACE所取得的成果，其实只是空军力量整体发展进程中的一个个环节罢了，”穆尔冈德说道。
穆尔冈德还研究了空军在推进ACE计划时的组织架构与运作方式。
空军成立了类似作战规划小组的ACE工作组，众多空军人员参与了这项工作，其中许多人仍需履行日常职责。
该工作组原本并不打算成为常设机构。
一旦达到某种稳定状态，就该将这项工作重新纳入常规的机构运作流程中，而非让其继续作为一项特殊举措存在，”穆尔冈德说道。
他认为到2024年秋季时，ACE已达到这一阶段。这一理念已被融入空军的作战条令、经费预算以及技术发展体系中。
解散该工作组是个正确的决定，”穆尔冈德说道。
虽然已经取得了一些进展，但仍有许多工作需要完成。”穆尔冈德表示。
我认为目前仍需着力解决的领域是各军种之间的协同整合，”穆尔冈德说道。
陆军采用多域作战模式，海军陆战队则运用远征型先进基地作战方式，而海军则实施分布式海上作战战略。这三支军种都各自探索出了适合自己的方法，旨在以更精简的兵力结构在多个作战领域形成强大的战斗力。
穆尔贡德表示，各军种接下来必须弄清楚这些作战方法该如何协同发挥作用。
他说：“通常的情况是，各军种首先会明确自己要执行的任务，之后再思考如何让这些任务在联合部队中协同发挥作用。
联合演习正是这一进程中的重要组成部分。
直到像‘竹鹰’这样的联合演习开展之后，各军种才真正开始理解其中的要点，”穆尔贡德说道，“因此，在推动各军种之间相互借鉴经验方面，我们仍有很多工作要做。
空军还通过与盟友及合作伙伴共同推进ACE项目的实施，积累了宝贵经验。
穆尔冈德指出，英国皇家空军、澳大利亚皇家空军以及加拿大皇家空军、法国空军和韩国空军都是正在努力解决如何在不同地点、不同条件下构建空中作战力量的类似问题的合作伙伴。
他在推动“敏捷作战运用”计划实施过程中的经验，也促使他开始研究另一个相关课题。
穆尔冈德正在撰写一本关于指挥与控制的书籍。他表示，关于指挥与控制的讨论往往集中在技术、通信系统以及具备韧性的网络架构上。
他说，这些因素固然重要，但单凭它们还不够。
穆尔冈德表示：‘的确，指挥与控制的这些方面至关重要。然而，它们仅凭自身无法推动指挥与控制体系向前发展。’
在穆尔冈德看来，问题的关键在于：在信息并不完备的情况下，人们该如何做出决策。
他说：“我们有必要回归指挥与控制的根本原则，也就是我在不确定环境下所强调的、由人类来做出决策这一关键环节。
技术会不断变化，作战环境亦然。穆尔甘德表示，不确定性仍将长期存在。
穆尔甘德表示：“不确定性、复杂性，以及各种障碍与摩擦，从来都不会消失，它们只会不断演变和变化。
这正是穆尔甘德希望在回顾ACE的实施情况之前先保持一定距离的原因之一。
下次全空军范围推行的相关举措不会与此次完全相同。穆尔甘德认为，负责推进这些举措的人员无需重新学习他的团队在将ACE理念引入空军作战体系过程中所积累的所有经验。
正因如此，这项工作才由空军大学来承担。
穆尔冈德将自己此前在推动全空军范围作战方式变革项目中所积累的经验带到了空军大学。空军大学出版社则承担起了将这些经验整理成文并提供给部队使用的出版工作。
这正是空军大学作为一体化机构运作的典范——它会根据具体任务需求，整合旗下各学院、研究中心及其他部门的资源。在本次案例中，出版工作有助于保存该作战行动中积累的经验教训；而对于其他不同类型的任务，则可能需要通过教育培训、科研分析、制定作战条令、模拟演练或借助专业技术力量来加以解决。
这种做法为空军大学培养具备专业能力的联合作战人员、并为联合部队解决作战难题的工作提供了有力支撑。
穆尔冈德的论文也留下了一些未解之谜。他指出，联合作战体系的整合仍是需要进一步努力的领域，同时他正在将自己从ACE项目中获得的经验运用到关于指挥控制的研究中，而该研究的重点则是探讨人们在不确定性环境下如何做出决策的问题。
对他而言，撰写这篇论文的原因其实更为简单。
他希望参与下一项计划的人员能够借鉴此次项目所积累的经验教训。

他并不想立刻着手进行这项工作。

2024年底相关工作结束后，穆尔冈德于2025年4月离开了空军参谋部。在回顾过往经验以及总结哪些经验能为后续承担类似任务的团队提供帮助之前，他希望先与这项工作保持一定距离。

穆尔冈德在空军大学出版社举办的作者交流活动中表示：“我并不太关注那些即时的战术反应，反而更希望随着时间推移回顾整个过程，将各项举措置于更宏观的背景中加以分析，从而获得更广阔的视野。

这一想法最终传到了空军大学。

2025年9月，穆尔贡德将这一想法向当时的空军大学司令安德里亚·图洛斯中将提出。空军大学通过其出版社出版了《实施新型空中力量概念：敏捷作战运用带来的启示》一书，对相关研究成果进行了整理记录。

穆尔贡德的目的并非仅记录有关“敏捷作战运用”这一概念的内容，他还想总结出那些经验教训，以便为后续试图在空军内部推广类似重大变革的团队提供参考。

穆尔贡德表示：“随着我们的作战理念、威胁环境以及新技术的不断演变，总会有新的任务需要去完成。我认为我们在推动‘敏捷作战运用’这一举措的过程中积累了一些经验，这些经验可供后续负责类似变革的团队借鉴，从而更快地推进他们手头的各项工作。

他说：“其中很大一部分工作就是学习如何协调整个空军范围内的大规模行动。

其中一些经验教训源自对更久远历史的回顾。

数十年来，空军一直习惯在几乎没有竞争的环境中，从大型固定基地出发来部署空中力量。但穆尔冈德找到了早期并非如此的实例作为对照。

他以驻扎在英格兰的第八空军、位于欧洲大陆的第九空军、道格拉斯·麦克阿瑟将军在南太平洋发动的岛链进攻行动，以及二战期间在中国作战的飞虎队作为参考案例。

这些部队还必须在面临威胁的作战环境下设法构建空中作战力量。

过去几年里我们通过ACE所取得的成果，其实只是空军力量整体发展进程中的一个个环节罢了，”穆尔冈德说道。

穆尔冈德还研究了空军在推进ACE计划时的组织架构与运作方式。

空军成立了类似作战规划小组的ACE工作组，众多空军人员参与了这项工作，其中许多人仍需履行日常职责。

该工作组原本并不打算成为常设机构。

一旦达到某种稳定状态，就该将这项工作重新纳入常规的机构运作流程中，而非让其继续作为一项特殊举措存在，”穆尔冈德说道。

解散该工作组是个正确的决定，”穆尔冈德说道。

虽然已经取得了一些进展，但仍有许多工作需要完成。”穆尔冈德表示。

items.title: Ragweed brings another round of seasonal allergies this fall
items.author: Maria Christina Yager
items.summary: FORT LEAVENWORTH, Kansas — If sneezing, congestion or itchy eyes have returned with the cooler weather, fall allergies may be responsible.
items.body: FORT LEAVENWORTH, Kansas — If sneezing, congestion or itchy eyes have returned with the cooler weather, fall allergies may be responsible. Although seasonal allergies are often associated with spring, ragweed is a common fall allergen. Symptoms may include sneezing, congestion, a runny nose, sinus pressure, headaches and red, watery or itchy eyes. Pollen may also trigger asthma symptoms in people who are sensitive to it. “Many people think allergy season ends with spring, but ragweed can cause symptoms well into the fall,” said Lt. Col. Baron Moehlenbrock, Munson Army Health Center chief of clinical services and a family nurse practitioner. “If your usual allergy symptoms return this time of year, you are not imagining it.” Outdoor activities, whether field exercises and ruck marching or mowing grass and raking leaves, can stir up pollen and increase exposure, which may worsen symptoms. People can’t necessarily avoid being outdoors, but remaining aware of pollen levels and taking appropriate action may help keep symptoms at bay. “The goal is not to stay inside all fall,” Moehlenbrock said. “A few simple habits can reduce how much pollen follows you indoors.” Showering and changing clothes after outdoor activities can remove pollen from the skin and hair. Keeping windows closed during periods of high pollen, washing hands before touching the eyes and using an appropriate high-efficiency home air filter may also help. For mild, occasional symptoms, TRICARE-eligible beneficiaries may obtain select over-the-counter allergy medications at no cost and without a prescription through the Munson Army Health Center Pharmacy’s Over The Counter Medication Program. The program is intended for short-term use. Beneficiaries with persistent or frequently recurring symptoms should contact their primary care manager. Schedule an appointment with your PCM if symptoms continue despite treatment, worsen, interfere with sleep or daily activities, or if a treatment that previously worked is no longer effective. Sudden or severe difficulty breathing is an emergency. Call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room if a person is struggling to breathe or speak, develops blue or gray lips or skin, feels faint or experiences swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat.
items.summaryZh: 堪萨斯州莱文沃思堡——如果天气转凉后又出现打喷嚏、鼻塞或眼睛发痒的症状，很可能是秋季过敏在作祟。
items.titleZh: 今秋豚草再度引发季节性过敏潮
zhParas: 堪萨斯州莱文沃思堡——如果天气转凉后又出现了打喷嚏、鼻塞或眼睛发痒的症状，很可能是秋季过敏在作祟。虽然季节性过敏通常与春季相关，但豚草是秋季常见的过敏原。其症状包括打喷嚏、鼻塞、流鼻涕、鼻窦压痛、头痛，以及眼睛发红、流泪或发痒。对花粉敏感的人还可能出现哮喘症状。芒森陆军医疗中心临床服务主管、家庭护士执业医师巴伦·莫伦布罗克中校表示：‘很多人以为过敏季在春季就结束了，但实际上豚草能引发的症状会持续到深秋。’‘如果每年这个时候都会出现熟悉的过敏症状，那绝非幻觉。’户外活动，无论是野外演习、负重行军，还是割草、扫落叶，都可能搅动花粉，增加接触机会，从而加重症状。虽然无法完全避免户外活动，但留意花粉浓度并采取适当措施有助于控制症状。莫伦布罗克说：‘目标并非整个秋季都待在室内，只要养成一些简单习惯，就能减少带入室内的花粉量。’户外活动后洗澡并更换衣物，可去除皮肤和头发上的花粉；在花粉浓度高的时候关闭窗户、触摸眼睛前先洗手，以及使用高效家用空气过滤器，也有助于缓解症状。对于轻微且偶尔出现的过敏症状，符合TRICARE保障资格的人可通过芒森陆军医疗中心药房的非处方药项目免费获取部分非处方抗过敏药物，该项目药物仅限短期使用。若症状持续或频繁复发，患者应联系自己的初级保健负责人。如果经过治疗症状仍无改善、反而加重，或影响到睡眠和日常活动，或是以往有效的疗法不再起作用，应预约初级保健负责人就诊。若出现突然或严重的呼吸困难，属于紧急情况，应立即拨打911或前往最近的急诊室，尤其是当患者呼吸困难或说话困难、嘴唇或皮肤呈现蓝色或灰色、感到头晕，或面部、嘴唇、舌头或喉咙出现肿胀时。

items.title: USACE Clears the Way for Coast Guard Readiness in St. Petersburg
items.author: Peggy Bebb
items.summary: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — A U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Jacksonville District team is dredging the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) boat basin in St. Petersburg, removing built-up sediment to improve access for Coast Guard crews to dock, maneuver within the basin, and deploy vessels more readily at low tide.
items.body:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — A U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Jacksonville District team is dredging the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) boat basin in St. Petersburg, removing built-up sediment to improve access for Coast Guard crews to dock, maneuver within the basin, and deploy vessels more readily at low tide.

"We are grateful to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers for its partnership and support in maintaining reliable access to the basin,” said Capt. Courtney Sergent, commanding officer of Coast Guard Sector St. Petersburg. “In addition to improving day-to-day access within the basin, the dredging project will help prepare the facility to receive a new Inland Construction Tender, part of the Coast Guard’s Waterways Commerce Cutter program, which will replace USCGC Vise. The new cutter's significantly greater draft further reinforces the need for dredging operations as the Coast Guard modernizes its aging fleet.”

It is a relatively small project, but the impact goes well beyond the basin. The work helps the Coast Guard stay ready for search and rescue, law enforcement, maritime security, emergency response and other missions along the Gulf Coast.

For the Coast Guard crews based in St. Petersburg, reliable access to the boat basin is not just convenient. It is part of being ready to respond when they are needed.

“The work we are performing is mechanical dredging to remove sediment that has built up in the Coast Guard’s boat basin,” said Steve Klemme, Jacksonville District Technical Support Branch Chief with the South Florida Operations Office, who is overseeing the field crew. “The project will help ensure Coast Guard vessels can get underway when needed by removing sediment that currently limits movement in the basin, particularly at lower tides.”

Once the work is complete, larger Coast Guard vessels will be able to use the station’s southern seawall and dock closer to the federal channel. That gives crews more flexibility and removes a restriction that can slow down vessel movements.

“This work will allow their larger vessels to be stationed closer to the federal channel and enhance the Coast Guard’s ability to respond to emergencies at a moment’s notice,” Klemme said.

That is why the project matters. Coast Guard personnel need to be able to get underway quickly for emergencies, security operations, law enforcement, environmental response and search-and-rescue missions. A shallow basin should not be the reason a vessel has to wait.

“Jacksonville District’s Operations Division is providing direct support to the Coast Guard to ensure their numerous mission sets, such as boat and vessel operations, safety and national security along the Gulf,” Operations Division Chief Tanner Clark said. “While USACE and USCG have distinctly different mission sets, we are primary partners and joint stakeholders toward ensuring everything from navigation, to security, to facility readiness, and of course public service to our citizens and to our great nation, the United States of America.”

One Team, Shared Mission

The project brings together people from across the Jacksonville District Operations Division and its South Florida Operations Office. Heavy-equipment operators, truck drivers, towboat personnel, mechanics, engineers, safety specialists, work leaders and administrative staff are all contributing to the same goal: helping Coast Guard crews stay ready.

“This team is unique for various reasons, but at the end of the day they are focused on accomplishing the mission,” Clark said. “They have numerous capabilities aligned with executing our operations and maintenance mission in South Florida, including multiple business lines like flood risk management and navigation. This project brought several staff together in multiple organizations within the Operations Division to support the Coast Guard.”

That kind of support is part of USACE’s larger operations and maintenance mission. USACE maintains navigation infrastructure, manages water resources, reduces flood risk and supports environmental stewardship. In St. Petersburg, the team is applying those same skills directly to a Coast Guard operational need.

“The team has a wide range of capabilities, and this project brought those capabilities together in support of another federal agency,” Clark said. “The work requires operational knowledge, technical expertise, field experience, engineering support and a strong safety culture. It is one team focused on one mission.”

Klemme said the work is a good match for the South Florida Operations Office team and its equipment. “Our team is happy to help any federal agency accomplish its mission,” Klemme said. “It just so happens that our equipment and team are suited to assist the Coast Guard with its mechanical dredging needs.”

The Coast Guard’s work affects people every day, whether they see it happening or not. Its crews protect ports and waterways, enforce laws at sea, support emergency response, safeguard the maritime environment and carry out security missions important to the nation’s economy and defense.

“The Jacksonville District crew knows what a vital asset the Coast Guard provides the United States by ensuring the borders and waterways are safe for the citizens and also their families,” Klemme said. “That is why the team takes this work seriously. We understand that helping the Coast Guard maintain access to its vessels helps support the people who protect our waterways and our nation.”

Planning for Reliable Access

Before the dredging started, the team had to answer some practical questions: How much sediment needed to come out? Where could the crew safely excavate? And where would the dredged material go?

“The engineering need was determining how much material needs to be removed for access to the dock, determining the limits of excavation and determining where to take the dredged fill,” Jacksonville District Project Engineer Keijo Hardin said. “The project was updated using a recent survey and the limits were established by the permit.”

That planning involved engineers, operations personnel and Coast Guard representatives. The team looked at survey data, permit conditions, excavation boundaries, waterfront structures, equipment staging areas, hauling routes and dredged-material requirements.

“The project is not simply a matter of putting equipment in the water and removing sediment,” Hardin said. “We follow the environmental requirements in the permit and engineering requirements, while confirming that the plans still meet the Coast Guard’s objective.”

USACE and Coast Guard personnel have stayed in close contact through planning and execution to make sure the work meets the Coast Guard’s needs while staying within environmental and engineering requirements.

“Follow-up meetings and questions onsite helped ensure all objectives were understood and agreed upon,” Hardin said. “The goal is to deliver a solution that is safe, buildable and useful to the Coast Guard.”

The result will be better access to the dock and southern seawall, more reliable movement in and out of the basin, and fewer restrictions caused by shoaling.

“Completing this project will enable the Coast Guard to traverse and dock more effectively at the station,” Hardin said.

The Crew Behind the Work

Mechanical dredging takes more than an excavator and a barge. It depends on a crew with different skills working together throughout the project.

“Our crew is so diverse that it takes all of their skills to accomplish this mission,” Klemme said. “We have several heavy-equipment operators that are digging the sediment and hauling it in dump trucks offsite. We have a mechanic that keeps all the equipment in top shape so that downtime is nonexistent.”

The towboat captain helps position the barge using the dredge survey, making sure operators are digging in the right places and staying within approved limits. Engineers, work leaders, safety personnel and administrative staff handle the planning, oversight and coordination that keep the operation moving.

“The towboat captain positions the barge according to the dredge survey to ensure we are digging in the correct spot,” Klemme said. “The support staff — work leaders, safety, engineers, administrative support and others — ensure all the administrative tasks are taken care of so that the crew can excel at what they do.”

The team starts each day with a safety meeting and equipment inspections before beginning work. Operators remove sediment, truck drivers haul it away and the mechanic moves between machines to keep them running. “The mechanic continually runs from every piece of equipment ensuring they are operating as intended,” Klemme said.

At the end of the day, the crew secures the towboat and barge, washes salt from the equipment, greases the machinery and reviews the day’s progress and any needed repairs.

“Around 1730 they will all meet in the galley of the towboat to meet about the day’s work and discuss items that need attention,” Klemme said. “Anything that needs repaired for the next day will be brought up to management, and they will formulate a plan to keep the program going forward.”

Safety Comes First

The worksite includes water, vessels, heavy equipment and moving trucks, so safety is part of every decision the crew makes.

“Completing the project in a safe and responsible manner is a priority of the Army Corps and its operators,” Hardin said. “We discuss safety and the project briefing daily. Personal protective equipment (PPE) is required for all operators and visitors.”

For the crew, safety is more than something covered at the start of the shift.

“Always wear your PPE anytime you are on the work site,” Klemme said. “If you see something, say something. Working near water has its challenges, and the crew is always prepared for worst-case scenario.” The team also must be ready to adjust when site conditions change.

“Their ability to adapt to currently changing conditions is something I am proud of,” Klemme said.

When the crew arrived one morning and found that the turbidity barrier had been moved, they had to quickly develop a plan to redeploy it so work could continue while protecting water quality Klemme said that willingness to step in wherever needed is one of the crew’s strengths.

“Most of the crew will always do anything necessary to accomplish the mission, even if it is not in their job description,” Klemme said. “They are mission-first teammates.”

Supporting a Federal Partner

The U.S. Coast Guard Sector St. Petersburg dredge project is an example of federal agencies using their different capabilities to support the same public-service mission. The Coast Guard brings maritime law enforcement, search and rescue, security and emergency-response expertise. USACE brings engineering, navigation, equipment and field operations capability.

“While USACE and USCG have distinctly different mission sets, we are primary partners and joint stakeholders,” Clark said. “We are working toward navigation, security, facility readiness and public service to our citizens and to our great nation.”

For the South Florida Operations Office team, the project also shows what the district can do when another federal partner needs help.

“It shows the ability of our South Florida Operations Office team to accomplish nearly any job that is brought to us,” Klemme said. “Most crews in other USACE districts have a specialty that they focus solely on, and our crew is willing to tackle any project that comes our way.

“It says a lot about the guys and also the leadership for stepping out of their comfort zone,” Klemme said. “We appreciate all opportunities to assist our federal partners.”

Hardin said the Coast Guard’s response has made the project especially meaningful.

“The most rewarding part of the project has been seeing and hearing from the Coast Guard members at the St. Petersburg station,” Hardin said. “You can tell that they are interested in and appreciate the work being completed.”

When the work is finished, the Coast Guard will have a deeper, more dependable boat basin, better access to the southern seawall and more flexibility to deploy vessels when needed.

For Klemme, though, success also means bringing everyone home safely.

“Success looks like all the guys return to the South Florida Operations Office safely and content,” Klemme said. “The Coast Guard is happy with the results of our work, USACE is happy that our schedules are met, and the crew learns at the same time.”

“These guys are not a professional dredge team,” Klemme added, “but with their basic skill sets and having the right equipment, we can accomplish anything.”

The dredging work at U.S. Coast Guard Sector St. Petersburg may be small in scale, but it reflects a bigger commitment: federal agencies supporting one another so the people responsible for protecting the nation have the access, equipment and readiness to respond when the country calls.
items.summaryZh: 佛罗里达州圣彼得斯堡——美国陆军工程兵团杰克逊维尔分部的一支队伍正在为圣彼得斯堡的美国海岸警卫队船只停泊区进行疏浚作业，清除堆积的沉积物，以便海岸警卫队人员更便利地进入码头、在停泊区内机动，同时在退潮时也能更轻松地派出船只执行任务。
items.titleZh: 美国陆军工程兵团为圣彼得斯堡海岸警卫队提升战备状态扫清障碍
zhParas: 佛罗里达州圣彼得斯堡——美国陆军工程兵团杰克逊维尔分部的一支队伍正在为圣彼得斯堡的美国海岸警卫队船只停泊区进行疏浚作业，清除堆积的沉积物，以便海岸警卫队人员更便利地进入码头、在停泊区内机动，同时在退潮时也能更轻松地派出船只执行任务。
虽然这只是一个规模相对较小的项目，但其影响却远不止于该船坞区域。这项工程有助于美国海岸警卫队保持良好的战备状态，从而更高效地执行墨西哥湾沿岸的搜救、执法、海上安全保障、应急响应等各类任务。
对于驻扎在圣彼得堡的美国海岸警卫队官兵而言，能够稳定地使用船坞并非仅仅是出于便利考虑，更是确保他们在需要时能够迅速响应、履行职责的关键条件。
一旦工程完工，规模更大的海岸警卫队舰艇将能够使用该站南侧的海堤，在更靠近联邦航道的位置停靠。这不仅为船员们提供了更大的操作灵活性，还能消除可能阻碍舰艇移动的种种限制。
克莱姆表示：“这项工程将使海岸警卫队的大型舰艇能够停靠在更靠近联邦航道的位置，同时提升其随时应对紧急情况的能力。
正因如此，这项工程才显得如此重要。海岸警卫队人员必须能够在紧急情况、安保行动、执法任务、环境应急以及搜救行动中迅速出动，而浅水船坞绝不能成为阻碍船只及时出发的障碍。
杰克逊维尔分区的行动部门正在为海岸警卫队提供直接支持，以确保其各项任务能够顺利开展，包括船只作业、海湾沿岸的安全保障以及国家安全工作。行动部门负责人坦纳·克拉克表示：‘尽管美国陆军工程兵团与海岸警卫队的任务各有不同，但我们在确保航行安全、设施战备状态以及为美国民众和整个美国提供公共服务等方面，都是重要的合作伙伴与共同责任方。’
一支队伍，共同的任务——美国陆军工程兵团杰克逊维尔分区的团队正在圣彼得堡为美国海岸警卫队的船只基地进行疏浚作业，清除积聚的沉积物，从而提升海岸警卫队人员进入码头、在基地内操作船只的便利性，使其能够更高效地部署舰艇执行任务。
这项工程汇集了杰克逊维尔分区作战部门及其南佛罗里达作战办公室的各类人员。重型设备操作员、卡车司机、拖船船员、机械师、工程师、安全专家、工作主管以及行政人员都在为同一个目标共同努力——确保海岸警卫队人员始终保持良好的战备状态。
克拉克表示，这支队伍因多种独特优势而备受重视，但归根结底他们始终以完成任务为首要目标。他们具备多种能力，可助力我们在南佛罗里达州开展各项运营与维护工作，涵盖洪水风险管控及航行保障等多领域业务。为支持海岸警卫队，该项目将运营部门下属不同机构的多名工作人员集结在一起协同作业。
此类支援属于美国陆军工程兵团更广泛的运营与维护任务范畴。该军团负责维护导航基础设施、管理水资源、降低洪水风险，并推动环境保护工作。在圣彼得斯堡，该团队正将同样的专业能力直接应用于满足海岸警卫队的作战需求。
克拉克表示：“该团队拥有多种专业能力，而这个项目正是将这些能力整合起来，为另一家联邦机构提供支持。这项工作需要运营知识、技术专长、实地经验、工程保障以及强烈的安全意识，整个团队都致力于完成同一项任务。
克莱姆表示，这项工作与南佛罗里达行动办公室的团队及其设备十分匹配。他称：“我们的团队很乐意协助任何联邦机构完成其任务，而恰好我们的设备与团队能力都适合为海岸警卫队的机械疏浚工作提供支持。
海岸警卫队的工作每天都在影响着每一个人，无论人们是否察觉。其官兵负责保护港口和水道、在海上执行执法任务、协助应急响应、维护海洋环境，同时还承担着对国家经济与国防至关重要的安保任务。
目前，美国陆军工程兵团杰克逊维尔分部团队正在为圣彼得堡的美国海岸警卫队船只停靠区进行疏浚作业，清除积聚的沉积物，旨在改善海岸警卫队人员进入码头、在停靠区内作业的便利性，同时提升船只的快速部署能力。
在开始疏浚作业之前，该团队必须先解决一些实际问题：需要清除多少沉积物？在哪些区域进行挖掘最为安全？而挖出的淤泥又该处置到何处？
杰克逊维尔分区的项目工程师凯乔·哈丁表示，这项工程任务主要包括确定为确保船只能够顺利进港需要清除多少沉积物、明确挖掘的边界范围，以及规划挖出的淤泥应堆放的地点。该项目的具体方案是根据最新的勘测数据制定的，而挖掘范围则由相关许可文件予以规定。
这项规划工作由工程师、作业人员以及美国海岸警卫队代表共同参与。团队仔细研究了相关勘测数据、许可要求、挖掘边界、滨水区域建筑、设备存放区、运输路线以及清淤量需求等各项因素。
在项目规划与实施过程中，美国陆军工程兵团与海岸警卫队人员保持着密切沟通，确保各项施工工作既能满足海岸警卫队的使用需求，又能符合相关的环境与工程标准。
这样一来，海岸警卫队人员就能更便捷地进出码头及南侧海堤，也能在船坞内更高效地移动，同时不必再受水深过浅带来的诸多限制。
哈丁表示：“该项目的完工将使海岸警卫队能够更高效地在该码头区域航行并停靠。
负责这项作业的工程团队正在为圣彼得堡的美国海岸警卫队船只停泊区进行疏浚作业，清除积聚的沉积物，以便海岸警卫队人员更便捷地进入码头、在停泊区内机动，同时也能更高效地派出船只执行任务。
机械疏浚作业绝非仅靠挖掘机和驳船就能完成，它需要一支具备多种专业技能的团队通力协作，全程推进各项作业。
克莱姆表示：‘我们的团队成员构成极为多元，要完成这项任务就需要发挥他们各自的专业技能。’他进一步说明：‘我们有几名重型设备操作员，负责挖掘沉积物并通过自卸卡车将其运出作业区域。此外还有一名机械师，确保所有设备始终处于最佳状态，从而杜绝设备故障带来的停机时间。’
拖船船长会根据疏浚作业的规划来调整驳船的位置，确保作业人员能在正确的地点进行挖掘，并始终保持在规定的作业范围内。与此同时，工程师、作业负责人、安全人员以及行政人员则负责整个作业的规划、监督与协调工作，以保证各项任务能够顺利推进。
克莱姆梅表示：‘拖船船长会根据疏浚作业的规划来调整驳船的位置，确保我们能在正确的地点进行挖掘。’他还称，‘那些后勤保障人员——包括作业负责人、安全人员、工程师、行政人员等——则负责处理所有行政事务，这样作业人员就能全神贯注地完成自己的工作。’
该工作小组每天开工前都会先召开安全会议并检查设备状况。操作人员负责清除沉积物，卡车司机将这些沉积物运走，而机械师则在各台设备间来回巡查，确保其正常运转。克莱姆表示：‘机械师会持续检查每一台设备，确保它们都能按预期工作。’
每天工作结束后，作业人员会固定好拖船和驳船，清除设备上的盐分，为机械部件加注润滑油，同时总结当天的工作进展并检查是否有需要维修的地方。
安全始终是首要考虑因素。
由于作业现场存在水域、各类船只、重型设备以及运输卡车，安全问题贯穿于工作人员做出的每一项决策之中。
哈丁表示，以安全且负责任的方式完成该项目是该工程兵团及其作业人员的首要任务。他们每天都会讨论安全问题并听取项目相关说明，所有作业人员及参观者都必须佩戴个人防护装备。
对相关船员而言，安全绝非仅在轮班开始时提及的事项。
克莱姆梅强调：“无论何时身处作业现场，都必须始终佩戴个人防护装备。一旦发现异常情况，应立即上报。在水域附近作业面临诸多挑战，全体人员必须随时做好应对最坏情况的准备。此外，当作业环境发生变化时，团队也必须能够迅速作出调整。
克莱姆梅表示：“他们能够适应当前不断变化的环境，这让我深感自豪。
当工作人员某天早晨抵达现场后，发现沉淀物屏障已被移动，他们不得不迅速制定计划重新设置该屏障，以便在保障水质的同时让工程工作得以继续。克莱姆梅表示，随时准备在需要时介入正是这支队伍的优势之一。
克莱姆梅表示：‘大多数船员始终会竭尽全力完成任务，即便这并非他们职责范围内的工作。他们是以任务为重的团队成员。’

美国海岸警卫队圣彼得堡辖区的疏浚项目，正是联邦各机构发挥自身不同优势、共同履行公共服务使命的典范。海岸警卫队具备海上执法、搜救、安保及应急响应等方面的专业能力，而美国陆军工程兵团则拥有工程建设、导航、设备供应以及实地作业方面的专业力量，二者通力协作以提升相关设施的可用性。
克拉克表示，尽管美国陆军工程兵团与美国海岸警卫队的任务定位各有不同，但双方仍是核心合作伙伴与共同利益攸关方。他们正共同努力，致力于保障航行安全、维护设施战备状态，同时为民众及整个国家提供优质公共服务。

工程完工后，海岸警卫队将拥有更深且更可靠的船只停泊区，能够更便捷地进入南侧海堤，同时在需要时也能更灵活地调度舰艇执行任务。

佛罗里达州圣彼得斯堡——美国陆军工程兵团杰克逊维尔分部的一支队伍正在为圣彼得斯堡的美国海岸警卫队船只停泊区进行疏浚作业，清除堆积的沉积物，以便海岸警卫队人员更便利地进入码头、在停泊区内机动，同时在退潮时也能更轻松地派出船只执行任务。



虽然这只是一个规模相对较小的项目，但其影响却远不止于该船坞区域。这项工程有助于美国海岸警卫队保持良好的战备状态，从而更高效地执行墨西哥湾沿岸的搜救、执法、海上安全保障、应急响应等各类任务。

对于驻扎在圣彼得堡的美国海岸警卫队官兵而言，能够稳定地使用船坞并非仅仅是出于便利考虑，更是确保他们在需要时能够迅速响应、履行职责的关键条件。



一旦工程完工，规模更大的海岸警卫队舰艇将能够使用该站南侧的海堤，在更靠近联邦航道的位置停靠。这不仅为船员们提供了更大的操作灵活性，还能消除可能阻碍舰艇移动的种种限制。

克莱姆表示：“这项工程将使海岸警卫队的大型舰艇能够停靠在更靠近联邦航道的位置，同时提升其随时应对紧急情况的能力。

正因如此，这项工程才显得如此重要。海岸警卫队人员必须能够在紧急情况、安保行动、执法任务、环境应急以及搜救行动中迅速出动，而浅水船坞绝不能成为阻碍船只及时出发的障碍。

杰克逊维尔分区的行动部门正在为海岸警卫队提供直接支持，以确保其各项任务能够顺利开展，包括船只作业、海湾沿岸的安全保障以及国家安全工作。行动部门负责人坦纳·克拉克表示：‘尽管美国陆军工程兵团与海岸警卫队的任务各有不同，但我们在确保航行安全、设施战备状态以及为美国民众和整个美国提供公共服务等方面，都是重要的合作伙伴与共同责任方。’

这项工程汇集了杰克逊维尔分区作战部门及其南佛罗里达作战办公室的各类人员。重型设备操作员、卡车司机、拖船船员、机械师、工程师、安全专家、工作主管以及行政人员都在为同一个目标共同努力——确保海岸警卫队人员始终保持良好的战备状态。

克拉克表示，这支队伍因多种独特优势而备受重视，但归根结底他们始终以完成任务为首要目标。他们具备多种能力，可助力我们在南佛罗里达州开展各项运营与维护工作，涵盖洪水风险管控及航行保障等多领域业务。为支持海岸警卫队，该项目将运营部门下属不同机构的多名工作人员集结在一起协同作业。

尽管在圣彼得堡海域进行的疏浚作业规模并不大，但它体现了更重要的承诺：各联邦机构之间相互支持，确保那些肩负国家保卫任务的人员能够拥有必要的通道、设备以及良好的战备状态，以便在国家面临危机时迅速作出反应。

items.title: Ready anywhere: How virtual wellness coaching fits military life
items.author: Douglas Holl
items.summary: Some service members may struggle to find time for their health and fitness goals while still meeting the many demands made on their schedules. The Armed Forces Wellness Center offers virtual health coaching to support military readiness, no matter where a client might be stationed. These AFWC virtual health programs provide personalized support without the burden of travel or scheduling conflicts.
items.body:
By Douglas Holl, Defense Health Agency-Public Health

Some service members may struggle to find time for their health and fitness goals while still meeting the many demands made on their schedules. The Armed Forces Wellness Center offers virtual health coaching to support military readiness, no matter where a client might be stationed. These AFWC virtual health programs provide personalized support without the burden of travel or scheduling conflicts.

Meeting clients where they are

For many service members, a demanding work schedule is the biggest barrier to staying fit and healthy. Army Master Sgt. Robert F. Nelson Jr., the logistics and supply noncommissioned officer in charge for Headquarters and Headquarters Company, 23rd Quartermaster Brigade, at Fort Lee, Virginia, knows this struggle firsthand. He turned to virtual coaching to help him manage weight control. Because sessions take place over the phone or online, clients don't need to spend time traveling to the AFWC at their installation.

"Virtual appointments made it extremely easy to manage my work schedule, other appointments, and get information I needed to meet my fitness goals," said Nelson. "There are many times that the constraints of my schedule have prevented me from seeking and getting the help I needed. These options made needed classes and assistance accessible."

Real results on a flexible timeline

Through the virtual program, Nelson received nutrition coaching and classes on food preparation. He was also able to complete body composition appointments at the Fort Lee AFWC. The flexible plan allowed him to stay on track. He lost 26 pounds, lowered his body mass index, and developed a cheaper meal preparation routine.

"It has made exercising easier and more effective," Nelson noted. "It has lowered my body mass index, which has helped to improve my health and stay within the Army standards."

He described his virtual collaboration with his coach as encouraging and supportive. "The coaches are knowledgeable, supportive, and realistic about my goals," said Nelson. "They provide encouragement and realistic expectations."

No cookie-cutter plans here

Some service members may worry that virtual healthcare lacks a personal touch, but AFWC health educators prove otherwise. Amy Ingersoll, an AFWC health educator at Fort Drum, New York, found that virtual sessions help build stronger connections.

"We do a lot of our virtual encounters over the phone," said Ingersoll. "I’ve noticed it seems easier to build trust and rapport because clients tend to be more open about what is going on with them when they don't have someone looking right at them for an extended period of time."

Ingersoll emphasized that every virtual coaching plan is highly customized. There is no one-size-fits-all plan. Client challenges could be fitness related, but often she finds herself addressing nutrition concerns.

“These concerns could be related to how much or what they are eating, or how to implement meal planning or meal prepping into their schedule,” said Ingersoll. “I’m working with someone right now whose goals are to reduce their soda intake and increase their water intake. That is what’s so great about health coaching in general, virtual or in-person, it’s tailored to exactly what the individual wants to accomplish.”

The AFWC client and virtual coach can meet weekly, biweekly, or monthly depending on their needs. If a client’s unit schedule changes, their coach can easily shift an appointment.

"You don't get the same plan or action steps as other clients," Ingersoll explained. "You may have similar goals, but how you choose to get there is up to you. You are the expert on your life and your situation."

AFWC health educators focus on client success

Ingersoll enjoys seeing clients meet their health and fitness goals.

“I love seeing how excited clients are when they’ve met the goal they’ve set,” said Ingersoll. “It is 100% their hard work and diligence that get them from point A to point B; I’m just lucky enough to be a partner in the process.”

Nelson encouraged anyone on the fence about using the program to take the leap.

"I would recommend that they give it a try despite any hesitation,” said Nelson. “The staff is professional and focused on helping you achieve your goals."

All Military Health System beneficiaries are eligible for Armed Forces Wellness Center services. This includes active duty service members and their families, retirees and spouses, and Department of War civilians.

Potential clients can learn more about AFWC services , including virtual health coaching, and locate the site nearest their installation by searching “Armed Forces Wellness Center” on the FindDHA site.

The Defense Health Agency is a Combat Support Agency, serving as a force multiplier for the joint services by optimizing lethality through warfighter medical readiness.

items.titleZh: 随时备战：虚拟健康辅导如何助力军人保持良好战备状态
zhParas: 据国防卫生局公共卫生部门道格拉斯·霍尔报道，为帮助军人在任何驻扎地点都能保持良好的战备状态，武装部队健康中心推出了虚拟健康辅导服务。由于军人的日程往往十分繁忙，他们可能难以抽出时间来实现自身的健康与健身目标，而这项虚拟辅导服务恰好能够为他们提供支持。
由于军人的日程往往十分繁忙，他们可能难以抽出时间来实现自身的健康与健身目标，而武装部队健康中心推出的虚拟健康辅导服务则能为他们提供支持，帮助其无论身处何地都能保持良好的战备状态。这些虚拟健康项目能够提供个性化的指导，让军人无需承担出行奔波或协调时间冲突的困扰。
无论军人身处何地，武装部队健康中心都能通过虚拟健康辅导服务为他们提供支持，帮助他们克服日程繁忙带来的困扰，从而持续维持良好的战备状态。
对许多军人而言，繁重的工作安排是保持健康体态的最大障碍。位于弗吉尼亚州李堡的第23军需旅司令部及司令部连的后勤与补给军士长罗伯特·F·纳尔逊就深有体会，他不得不面对因工作繁忙而难以兼顾健康问题的困境。为了解决体重控制的问题，他选择了虚拟健康辅导服务——由于辅导是通过电话或网络进行的，军人无需特意前往所在驻地的武装部队健康中心即可接受服务。
纳尔逊表示：‘通过虚拟预约，我能够非常轻松地协调工作安排和其他事务，同时获取实现健身目标所需的信息。’他进一步指出：‘很多时候，繁重的日程安排让我无法寻求所需的帮助。而虚拟服务让这些必要的课程和辅导变得触手可及。’
在灵活的时间安排下依然能取得切实成效。
通过这项虚拟健康服务，纳尔逊获得了营养指导以及烹饪课程，同时还能够在李堡的AFWC中心进行身体成分检测。灵活的服务安排让他能够坚持计划执行，最终减重26磅，体质量指数也有所下降，同时还找到了成本更低的膳食准备方法。
纳尔逊表示，这种虚拟健康辅导服务让锻炼变得更轻松、更有效。它帮助我降低了体质量指数，进而提升了我的健康状况，也让我符合军队的健康标准。
纳尔逊表示，他与虚拟健康教练的协作过程充满鼓励与支持。‘这些教练知识渊博，态度积极，还能对我设定的目标保持现实认知，’他说道，‘他们会给予我鼓励，同时设定切实可行的期望。’
这里并没有千篇一律的标准方案。
虽然有些军人担心虚拟医疗服务缺乏人际互动的亲切感，但AFWC的健康指导员们却证明了并非如此。位于纽约德拉姆堡的AFWC健康指导员艾米·英格索尔发现，通过虚拟方式进行的咨询反而有助于建立更牢固的信任关系。
英格索尔表示：‘我们的许多虚拟咨询都是通过电话进行的。’她发现，这种方式更容易建立信任与融洽的关系，因为当客户无需面对他人的目光时，他们往往更愿意敞开心扉，讲述自己的状况。’
英格索尔强调，每份虚拟健康指导计划都是高度定制化的，并不存在适用于所有人的统一方案。客户的困扰可能涉及健身方面，但她常常需要解决他们的营养问题。
英格索尔表示，这些困扰可能源于他们的饮食量或饮食内容，或是如何在繁忙的日程中安排饮食计划或提前准备食物。我目前正在为一名希望减少汽水摄入量并增加饮水量的军人提供指导。正因如此，无论是虚拟还是面对面的健康辅导都如此出色——它们都能根据个人的具体目标来量身定制相应的方案。
AFWC的服务对象与虚拟健康教练可根据自身需求选择每周、每两周或每月进行一次会面。如果服务对象的部队任务安排发生变化，教练也能轻松调整会面时间。
英格索尔解释说：‘你不会和其他客户获得相同的计划或行动方案。’他进一步指出：‘虽然你们的目标可能相似，但实现目标的具体方式由你自己决定。你才是最了解自己生活状况和处境的人。’
AFWC的健康指导专家们致力于帮助服务人员实现健康目标。
英格索尔很高兴看到客户们能够实现自己的健康与健身目标。
纳尔逊鼓励那些还在犹豫是否使用该项目的军人勇敢尝试。
纳尔逊表示：‘尽管可能存在些许犹豫，但我仍建议他们不妨试一试。’他补充道，‘那里的工作人员专业素养极高，且一心致力于帮助人们实现健康目标。’
所有军事医疗体系的受益人均有资格享受武装部队健康中心提供的服务，这包括现役军人及其家属、退役军人及其配偶，以及国防部所属的文职人员。
潜在服务对象可通过FindDHA网站搜索“Armed Forces Wellness Center”，了解更多关于武装部队健康中心所提供的服务信息，包括虚拟健康辅导服务，同时还能查找距离其驻扎地最近的服务中心位置。
国防卫生局属于作战支援机构，通过提升军人战备状态来增强其作战能力，进而为各军种协同作战发挥助力作用。

items.body:
MOBILE, Ala. — For 34 years, one constant inside the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Mobile District has been the steady, dedicated leadership of Julie Walton. While her roots remained firmly planted along the banks of Mobile Bay for more than three decades, her professional footprint spanned high-stakes national defense initiatives and an entire hemisphere of international cooperation.

Surrounded by colleagues, and leadership during her recent retirement ceremony at the Mobile District headquarters, Walton, the OCONUS IIS Branch Chief and the Latin America Program Manager, officially brought a distinguished 34-year federal civil service career to a close.

Highlighting the ceremony was the presentation of the prestigious Bronze Order of the de Fleury Medal—one of the highest honors in the Army Engineer Regiment—recognizing her enduring contributions to USACE, national defense, and international partner nations.

“It has truly been a privilege to work with a team of professionals from across the district and across the region who are the definition of selfless service and dedication," Walton noted.

Sparking a Passion: From Cape Canaveral to Advanced Engineering

Walton’s 34-year journey with Mobile District began not in an executive suite, but at the drafting and design table solving complex technical challenges. Looking back across her career, she points to her early days as a mechanical specialties designer as the crucible that shaped her technical path.

Early on, Walton served on the multidisciplinary engineering team tasked with a full design retrofit of fire sprinkler systems for the U.S. Air Force Vertical Integration Building (VIB) and Launch Operations Control Center at Cape Canaveral, Florida.

"I have been fortunate enough to have had some really amazing experiences during my career, but I think I’ll go way back to the first major project I worked on as a mechanical specialties designer," Walton recalled. "It created for me a love of fire protection engineering that led to pursuing a graduate degree in the field."

The technical rigor required for space-launch infrastructure left an indelible mark on her approach to problem-solving.

"I was part of the team that did a full design for retrofitting sprinkler systems into the USAF Vertical Integration Building and Launch Operations Control Center at Cape Canaveral," she said. "The lessons I learned both during the design process and from the installers during construction as we resolved design issues have stuck with me to this day."

Managing High-Tempo Missions: MEDCOM, DHA, and LATAM

As her career evolved, Walton transitioned her technical precision into large-scale project and program management. The bulk of her three decades was defined by two demanding and vital mission sets: supporting military healthcare facilities through the U.S. Army Medical Command (MEDCOM) and the Defense Health Agency (DHA), and directing operations throughout Latin America . Formally serving as the Branch Chief for Outside the Continental United States (OCONUS) Interagency and International Services (IIS) within the Programs and Project Management Division (PPMD)—known colloquially across the region as the Latin America Program Manager—Walton directed complex engineering and construction portfolios in support of U.S. Southern Command (USSOUTHCOM), partner nation militaries, and U.S. embassies across Central and South America.

The OCONUS IIS portfolio routinely translated strategic bilateral priorities into disaster relief warehouses, emergency operations centers, maritime bases, medical clinics, and school renovations.

Andre Lucy, Chief MEDCOM Support Section, said Walton’s expertise will be sorely missed in the Mobile District.

“Julie Walton was one of the pillars of the foundation of our Medical Support Team here in the Mobile District when our primary customer was the Army’s Medical Command (MEDCOM),” Lucy said. “Though her title was Project Manager, she functioned as a true Program Manager, steering Contracting and Project Management for both Construction and Operations & Maintenance (O&M) programs with integrity and accountability. Through her leadership, the MST was setup for success when the medical programs for all uniformed services were transitioned from MEDCOM and other branches to the Defense Health Agency. Whenever you meet someone across Medical Command or DHA who knows Julie, they share the exact same sentiment: high praise, deep respect, and admiration for her exceptional leadership.”

"A Microcosm of the District"

Managing engineering operations across international boundaries brought logistical, linguistic, and geopolitical complexities that few domestic offices encounter. Yet, Walton always viewed the Latin America program as an integral reflection of Mobile District’s broader capabilities.

"I’ve always described the Latin America program as a microcosm of the district," Walton explained. "Almost everything Mobile District does, we’ve done to some extent in LATAM at some point in time. That makes for a very diverse and dynamic workload executed across a huge geography with multiple unique cultures, languages, and political situations."

Despite the challenging operating environments, Walton credited the team on the ground for sustaining mission success year after year.

Lisa Grande, Mobile District Deputy Chief for Programs and Project Management, said Walton’s career was one that ensured the District’s success.

“Julie’s leadership ensured the Mobile District’s success in the delivery of critical infrastructure and interagency technical assistance programs across Central and South America,” Grande said. “She expertly navigated the strategic impacts and political sensitivities of engaging with foreign governments and leaders at multiple levels within the Department of Defense and Department of State.”

Rebecca Whiteside, Architect and Project Manager for LATAM and the newest member of the team said Walton will be missed.

“Julie and everyone on the team, were very patient with me and generous of their time to help me transition from EN to PM,” Whiteside said. “She always had an open door to help resolve any issue that we encountered. I have always been fascinated with Julie’s extensive knowledge or the many different rules and regulations regarding the numerous funding sources that the LATAM Program worked with. She will be irreplaceable. Her knowledge, work ethic, demeanor and friendliness will be missed by all of us that worked with her.”

The True Bedrock: Family and Shared Sacrifice

Behind 34 years of mission execution was a demanding tempo of frequent international travel and intense fourth-quarter fiscal year-end deadlines. Walton readily acknowledges that her achievements were made possible only through the steadfast support of her family.

"With the bulk of my career spent supporting the MEDCOM/DHA and LATAM programs, travel has been a significant part of my routine," Walton shared. "Between that and long hours in the fourth quarter of each fiscal year, my husband had to take on more than his fair share of the load to keep the household running smoothly."

Her husband, Tommy Walton, and their three children—Emily, Ryan, and Nicholas—became the silent partners in her decades of service.

"My family has never questioned or complained when I had to miss an event or shift schedules when necessary," said Walton. "I can’t imagine juggling work and family without that kind of support."

Charting the Course: Advice to the Next Generation

Having navigated a 34-year career entirely within one district while continually reinventing her professional portfolio, Walton offers pragmatic advice to early-career engineers and civilian professionals stepping into USACE:

"Early in your career, set long-term professional goals for what you would like to accomplish in your career," Walton advised. "The value isn’t in working toward those specific goals, but in understanding that what you do today impacts your future. USACE offers many different paths and experiences, so be intentional about the course you chart."

Honored with the de Fleury Medal and Fond Farewells

The presentation of the Bronze Order of the de Fleury Medal served as a fitting culmination to Walton's service. Named in honor of François-Louis Teissèdre de Fleury, the French engineer who distinguished himself at the 1779 Battle of Stony Point, the medal honors individuals who have provided significant, lasting contributions to the U.S. Army Engineer Regiment.

Aimee McCormick, MEDCOM Program Manager, said Walton’s consistency and dedication will always be remembered.

“Julie is an exemplary leader who consistently guides her team by example,” McCormick said. “During our time working together while she served as the MEDCOM Program Manager, I was thoroughly impressed by her dedication. She is highly collaborative, proactively addressing challenges and supporting colleagues across all levels of the organization. Julie consistently exceeds expectations and delivers outstanding results.”

As she reflected on the medal, the milestones, and the infrastructure built across multiple continents, Walton concluded that the true legacy of her 34 years comes down to camaraderie.

"Every retiree says it, but they say it because it’s true: I will miss my USACE family," Walton said. "It’s the people you meet and the friendships you build that matter in the end."
items.summaryZh: 阿拉巴马州莫比尔市——34年来，美国陆军工程兵团莫比尔分部之所以能够保持稳定高效的运作，离不开朱莉·沃尔顿始终如一的卓越领导。尽管她在莫比尔湾沿岸工作了三十多年，但她的职业足迹却遍布各种至关重要的国防项目，同时还参与了覆盖整个美洲大陆的国际合作事务。在莫比尔分部总部举行的退休仪式上，她在同事们及上级领导的见证下完成了职业生涯的最后一程。
items.titleZh: 扎根莫比尔，影响遍美洲：朱莉·沃尔顿在34年勤勉服务后退休
zhParas: 阿拉巴马州莫比尔市——34年来，美国陆军工程兵团莫比尔分部始终保持着稳定而高效的运作，其背后离不开朱莉·沃尔顿始终如一的卓越领导。尽管她在莫比尔湾沿岸工作了三十多年，但她的职业足迹却遍布各种至关重要的国防项目，同时还参与了覆盖整个美洲大陆的国际合作事务。
在莫比尔分部总部举行的退休仪式上，朱莉·沃尔顿在同事们及上级领导的见证下，正式结束了她长达34年的联邦公务员生涯。作为海外第二类驻地的分支主管兼拉丁美洲项目负责人，她始终以卓越的领导力为该部门的发展奠定坚实基础。
在举行的退休仪式上，最引人注目的环节是为朱莉·沃尔顿颁发了享有盛誉的德弗勒里勋章铜级奖章，这是美国陆军工程兵团授予的最高荣誉之一，旨在表彰她为该机构、国家国防事业以及国际合作伙伴国家所做出的长期贡献。
沃尔顿表示：“能够与来自该地区乃至更广阔范围的众多专业团队共事，真是我的荣幸。他们都是无私奉献、恪尽职守的典范。
从卡纳维拉尔角到先进工程领域：点燃热情的职业生涯
沃尔顿在美军工程兵团莫比尔分区的34年职业生涯并非从办公室领导岗位起步，而是从解决复杂技术难题的绘图设计岗位开始的。回顾自己的职业生涯，她认为自己早年间作为机械专业设计师的那段经历，正是塑造其技术发展道路的关键阶段。
早年，沃尔顿曾加入一个多学科工程团队，负责对美国空军垂直整合大楼以及位于佛罗里达州卡纳维拉尔角的发射操作控制中心内的消防喷淋系统进行全面的设计改造工作。
沃尔顿回忆道：“在我的职业生涯中，我有幸经历过许多非常精彩的经历，但若要追溯最让我难忘的，当属我最初作为机械设计专家参与的那个重大项目。正是那个项目让我爱上了消防工程，也促使我后来攻读了该领域的研究生学位。
航天发射基础设施所要求的高标准技术要求，让她在解决问题的方式上留下了难以磨灭的深刻影响。
我曾参与那个团队，为美国空军位于卡纳维拉尔角的垂直整合大楼以及发射操作控制中心设计喷淋系统的升级方案，”她说道，“无论是设计阶段积累的经验，还是施工过程中与安装人员共同解决各种设计问题时所学到的知识，至今仍深深印在我的脑海中。
在应对节奏迅速的各项任务时，美军欧洲司令部、国防创新单元以及拉丁美洲司令部始终发挥着关键作用，共同确保各项军事行动能够高效、有序地推进。

在职业生涯的发展过程中，沃尔顿将自身的技术专长转化为大规模项目与计划管理能力。在长达三十年的工作中，她主要负责两项至关重要且任务艰巨的工作：通过美国陆军医疗司令部及国防卫生局为各类军事医疗设施提供支持，同时负责整个拉丁美洲地区的行动指挥。她曾担任计划与项目管理处“美国本土以外地区跨机构及国际服务”部门的负责人——该职位在该地区通常被称为“拉丁美洲项目负责人”——负责统筹各类复杂的工程与建设项目，为美国南方司令部、各合作国家军队以及分布在中美洲和南美洲的美国大使馆提供支持。
作为负责美国本土以外地区跨机构及国际服务的核心项目，该计划组长期将各项战略性的双边合作重点转化为实际的救援设施——包括救灾仓库、应急行动中心、海上基地、医疗诊所以及学校翻修项目等。
美军欧洲司令部医疗支援科科长安德烈·露西表示，莫比尔军区将会极为怀念沃尔顿的专业素养与贡献。

露西表示：‘在莫比尔军区，当我们的主要服务对象还是陆军医疗司令部时，朱莉·沃尔顿就是我们医疗支援团队建设的核心支柱之一。’尽管她的职位是项目经理，但实际上她更像是一名真正的项目主管，以高度的诚信与责任感负责各类建设及运维项目的合同管理与人事统筹工作。在所有军种的医疗事务从陆军医疗司令部及其他部门移交至国防卫生局之后，正是在她的领导下，该医疗支援团队才得以顺利运转并取得成功。无论是在陆军医疗司令部还是国防卫生局，凡是认识朱莉的人，都对她的卓越领导力给予极高的评价、深深的敬意与由衷的钦佩。’
作为该军事管区的缩影，朱莉·沃尔顿34年的勤勉履职为这里留下了深远影响。
负责管理跨越国界的工程作业，意味着要应对诸多国内办公室几乎不会遇到的后勤、语言及地缘政治方面的复杂问题。然而，沃尔顿始终将拉丁美洲地区的工程项目视为莫比尔军区整体能力的体现。
沃尔顿解释说：“我一直将拉丁美洲的项目视为该军区的一个缩影。莫比尔军区开展的几乎所有工作，我们在拉丁美洲也都曾在不同程度上开展过。因此，这里的工作任务极为多样且充满变化，需要在幅员辽阔、拥有多种独特文化、语言及政治环境的地区来执行。
尽管面临诸多艰巨的作业环境，沃尔顿仍将任务能够年复一年地顺利完成归功于一线团队的不懈努力。
莫比尔区项目与计划管理副主任丽莎·格兰德表示，沃尔顿的职业生涯为该区的成功奠定了坚实基础。
格兰德表示，正是朱莉的领导力确保了莫比尔区能够成功在中美洲和南美洲推进各类关键基础设施建设以及跨机构技术援助项目。她还擅长应对与国防部及国务院各级外国政府及领导人打交道时所面临的战略层面影响与政治敏感性问题。
负责拉丁美洲项目的架构师兼项目经理、也是该团队最新加入的成员丽贝卡·怀特赛德表示，大家将会十分怀念朱莉·沃尔顿。
怀特赛德表示：‘朱莉以及团队里的每一个人都对我非常有耐心，还慷慨地抽出时间帮助我完成从工程师到项目经理的转型。每当遇到问题，她总是敞开大门为我提供帮助。我一直很钦佩朱莉渊博的知识，以及她对LATAM项目所涉及的各类资金来源相关的各种规章制度了如指掌。她是个无可替代的人，她的专业知识、工作态度、处事方式以及友善的性格，都会让我们所有与她共事过的人深深怀念。’
对于朱莉·沃尔顿而言，家庭以及大家共同做出的牺牲才是最坚实的支撑。34年的辛勤工作背后，始终有着家人的默默陪伴与支持，而她在工作中所展现出的奉献精神，也离不开同事们共同分担的重任与牺牲。正是这份家庭与团队的紧密纽带，让她能够在漫长的服役生涯中始终保持坚定的信念与动力。
在34年的任务执行历程背后，是频繁的国际出差以及财年第四季度紧迫的截止日期所带来的高强度工作节奏。沃尔顿坦言，自己的所有成就离不开家人的坚定支持。
沃尔顿表示：“在我的职业生涯中，大部分时间都用于支持美军欧洲司令部及拉丁美洲相关项目，因此出差已成为我日常工作的重要组成部分。再加上每个财年第四季度繁重的工作任务，我的丈夫不得不承担超出常理的家庭责任，才能确保家庭生活平稳运转。
她的丈夫汤米·沃尔顿以及他们的三个孩子——艾米丽、瑞安和尼古拉斯——成为了她数十载服役生涯中默默的支持者。
沃尔顿表示：“每当我有必要缺席某些活动或调整工作日程时，我的家人从未有过质疑或抱怨。没有这样的支持，我根本无法同时兼顾工作和家庭。
规划未来之路：给下一代的建议
在同一个军区工作了34年期间，朱莉·沃尔顿不断更新自己的专业技能与职责范围，同时始终保持着稳定的领导风格。如今退役之际，她为那些刚入伍的工程师以及即将加入美国陆军工程兵团的文职人员提供了实用的建议。
沃尔顿建议：“在职业生涯初期，就应该为自己设定长远的专业目标。”她指出，“重要的并非一味追求那些具体目标，而是要明白自己今天的每一项行动都会影响未来。美国陆军工程兵团提供了众多不同的发展路径与实践机会，因此务必认真规划自己的职业方向。
朱莉·沃尔顿因卓越的贡献而荣获德弗勒里奖章，同时在告别仪式上也收到了众多人的深情祝福。
德弗勒里奖章的铜级勋章的授予，为沃尔顿34年的奉献生涯画上了完美的句号。该勋章以在1779年斯托尼点战役中表现突出的法国工程师弗朗索瓦-路易·特塞德·德弗勒里命名，旨在表彰那些为美国陆军工程兵团作出重大且持久贡献的人士。
美军欧洲司令部MEDCOM项目负责人艾米·麦考密克表示，人们将永远铭记沃尔顿一贯的专注与奉献精神。
在回顾那些荣誉奖章、重要里程碑以及她在各大洲推动建设的基础设施时，沃尔顿认为，自己34年服务生涯留下的真正遗产，其实就是军人们之间的深厚情谊。
沃尔顿表示：‘每位退休人员都会这么说，而他们这么说是因为事实确实如此——我会想念我在美国陆军工程兵团的家人。归根结底，重要的其实是那些你结识的人以及你们之间建立的友谊。’

作为负责美国本土以外地区跨机构及国际服务的核心项目，该计划组长期将各项战略性的双边合作重点转化为实际的救援设施——包括救灾仓库、应急行动中心、海上基地、医疗诊所以及学校翻修项目等。

美军欧洲司令部医疗支援科科长安德烈·露西表示，莫比尔军区将会极为怀念沃尔顿的专业素养与贡献。

露西表示：‘在莫比尔军区，当我们的主要服务对象还是陆军医疗司令部时，朱莉·沃尔顿就是我们医疗支援团队建设的核心支柱之一。’尽管她的职位是项目经理，但实际上她更像是一名真正的项目主管，以高度的诚信与责任感负责各类建设及运维项目的合同管理与人事统筹工作。在所有军种的医疗事务从陆军医疗司令部及其他部门移交至国防卫生局之后，正是在她的领导下，该医疗支援团队才得以顺利运转并取得成功。无论是在陆军医疗司令部还是国防卫生局，凡是认识朱莉的人，都对她的卓越领导力给予极高的评价、深深的敬意与由衷的钦佩。’

作为该军事管区的缩影，朱莉·沃尔顿34年的勤勉履职为这里留下了深远影响。

负责管理跨越国界的工程作业，意味着要应对诸多国内办公室几乎不会遇到的后勤、语言及地缘政治方面的复杂问题。然而，沃尔顿始终将拉丁美洲地区的工程项目视为莫比尔军区整体能力的体现。

沃尔顿解释说：“我一直将拉丁美洲的项目视为该军区的一个缩影。莫比尔军区开展的几乎所有工作，我们在拉丁美洲也都曾在不同程度上开展过。因此，这里的工作任务极为多样且充满变化，需要在幅员辽阔、拥有多种独特文化、语言及政治环境的地区来执行。

尽管面临诸多艰巨的作业环境，沃尔顿仍将任务能够年复一年地顺利完成归功于一线团队的不懈努力。

莫比尔区项目与计划管理副主任丽莎·格兰德表示，沃尔顿的职业生涯为该区的成功奠定了坚实基础。

格兰德表示，正是朱莉的领导力确保了莫比尔区能够成功在中美洲和南美洲推进各类关键基础设施建设以及跨机构技术援助项目。她还擅长应对与国防部及国务院各级外国政府及领导人打交道时所面临的战略层面影响与政治敏感性问题。

负责拉丁美洲项目的架构师兼项目经理、也是该团队最新加入的成员丽贝卡·怀特赛德表示，大家将会十分怀念朱莉·沃尔顿。

怀特赛德表示：‘朱莉以及团队里的每一个人都对我非常有耐心，还慷慨地抽出时间帮助我完成从工程师到项目经理的转型。每当遇到问题，她总是敞开大门为我提供帮助。我一直很钦佩朱莉渊博的知识，以及她对LATAM项目所涉及的各类资金来源相关的各种规章制度了如指掌。她是个无可替代的人，她的专业知识、工作态度、处事方式以及友善的性格，都会让我们所有与她共事过的人深深怀念。’

对于朱莉·沃尔顿而言，家庭以及大家共同做出的牺牲才是最坚实的支撑。34年的辛勤工作背后，始终有着家人的默默陪伴与支持，而她在工作中所展现出的奉献精神，也离不开同事们共同分担的重任与牺牲。正是这份家庭与团队的紧密纽带，让她能够在漫长的服役生涯中始终保持坚定的信念与动力。

在34年的任务执行历程背后，是频繁的国际出差以及财年第四季度紧迫的截止日期所带来的高强度工作节奏。沃尔顿坦言，自己的所有成就离不开家人的坚定支持。

沃尔顿表示：“在我的职业生涯中，大部分时间都用于支持美军欧洲司令部及拉丁美洲相关项目，因此出差已成为我日常工作的重要组成部分。再加上每个财年第四季度繁重的工作任务，我的丈夫不得不承担超出常理的家庭责任，才能确保家庭生活平稳运转。

她的丈夫汤米·沃尔顿以及他们的三个孩子——艾米丽、瑞安和尼古拉斯——成为了她数十载服役生涯中默默的支持者。

沃尔顿表示：“每当我有必要缺席某些活动或调整工作日程时，我的家人从未有过质疑或抱怨。没有这样的支持，我根本无法同时兼顾工作和家庭。

规划未来之路：给下一代的建议

在同一个军区工作了34年期间，朱莉·沃尔顿不断更新自己的专业技能与职责范围，同时始终保持着稳定的领导风格。如今退役之际，她为那些刚入伍的工程师以及即将加入美国陆军工程兵团的文职人员提供了实用的建议。

沃尔顿建议：“在职业生涯初期，就应该为自己设定长远的专业目标。”她指出，“重要的并非一味追求那些具体目标，而是要明白自己今天的每一项行动都会影响未来。美国陆军工程兵团提供了众多不同的发展路径与实践机会，因此务必认真规划自己的职业方向。

朱莉·沃尔顿因卓越的贡献而荣获德弗勒里奖章，同时在告别仪式上也收到了众多人的深情祝福。

德弗勒里奖章的铜级勋章的授予，为沃尔顿34年的奉献生涯画上了完美的句号。该勋章以在1779年斯托尼点战役中表现突出的法国工程师弗朗索瓦-路易·特塞德·德弗勒里命名，旨在表彰那些为美国陆军工程兵团作出重大且持久贡献的人士。

美军欧洲司令部MEDCOM项目负责人艾米·麦考密克表示，人们将永远铭记沃尔顿一贯的专注与奉献精神。



在回顾那些荣誉奖章、重要里程碑以及她在各大洲推动建设的基础设施时，沃尔顿认为，自己34年服务生涯留下的真正遗产，其实就是军人们之间的深厚情谊。

沃尔顿表示：‘每位退休人员都会这么说，而他们这么说是因为事实确实如此——我会想念我在美国陆军工程兵团的家人。归根结底，重要的其实是那些你结识的人以及你们之间建立的友谊。’

items.title: Aircraft Program Management Office Welcomes New Program Manager
items.author: Courtesy
items.summary: NAVAL AIR SYSTEMS COMMAND, PATUXENT RIVER, Md. – The Navy’s Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager for Robotic and Autonomous Systems welcomed Col. Matthew Allen as its new program manager during a change of command ceremony held last month at the RADM William A. Moffett Building at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland.
items.body:
NAVAL AIR SYSTEMS COMMAND, PATUXENT RIVER, Md. – The Navy’s Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager for Robotic and Autonomous Systems welcomed Col. Matthew Allen as its new program manager during a change of command ceremony held last month at the RADM William A. Moffett Building at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland.

Chris Miller, DRPM RAS, presided over the ceremony during which Allen relieved Gregg Skinner, who led the Aircraft Program Management Office (AIR PMO) through a period of continued growth in Navy and Marine Corps unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) capabilities.

“This team has an important mission, and Gregg, your leadership has been the bedrock of this team,” said Christopher Miller, DRPM RAS. “As much as Gregg has led the charge to deliver capability to the fleet at extraordinary speed, he has also built a high-performing, resilient team.”

During Skinner’s tenure, the Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance Services program surpassed one million flight hours supporting operations on land and at sea. Since its inception in 2005, the program completed more than 50 UAS installations aboard Navy and Military Sealift Command ships and has operated from more than 50 land-based locations worldwide.

The AIR PMO team also supported the delivery of 4,480 Family of Small UAS air vehicles during the last 12 months and expects 1,520 additional air vehicles this winter to support of Drone Dominance. The team advanced the Navy’s first shipboard manned-unmanned teaming capability, completed shipboard testing of the TRV-150C Tactical Resupply Unmanned Aircraft System, and awarded Medium Aerial Resupply Vehicle Expeditionary Logistics Other Transaction Authorities to two vendors for the next phase of unmanned logistics prototyping.

“A change of command is an inheritance,” said Skinner. “None of us created everything we were given. We inherited organizations, relationships, knowledge, traditions, hard-earned lessons and trust, and people who had invested years of their lives in the mission before we arrived.”

A career Marine officer, Allen has led operational, maintenance, logistics, and acquisition teams across infantry, aviation maintenance, small tactical unmanned aircraft systems, and shore air traffic management. He previously served in leadership roles with the Presidential Helicopters program office, Marine Aviation Logistics Squadrons 29 and 31, Marine Fighter Attack Squadron 312, Shore Air Traffic Management, and the Office of the Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Navy-Air/Ground.

From 2017 to 2021, Allen served with AIR PMO, formerly the Navy and Marine Corps Small Tactical Unmanned Aircraft Systems program office (PMA 263), where he led rapid prototyping efforts for the Unmanned Logistics System-Air and served as the RQ-21A Blackjack military integrated product lead. He is a certified Project Management Professional with advanced acquisition certifications in Life Cycle Logistics and Program Management.

In his remarks, Allen reflected on returning to lead the organization where he previously served and addressed the AIR PMO team and the path ahead.

“We will stay laser-focused on speed to fleet,” said Allen. “The pacing threat demands that we make these systems available, modular, and survivable right now.”

DRPM RAS is responsible for the development, requirements, and acquisition of RAS capabilities across the Department of the Navy. For more information on DRPM RAS, visit drpmras.navy.mil

items.titleZh: 海军航空系统司令部项目管理办公室任命新任项目经理
zhParas: 马里兰州帕图森特河的海军航空系统司令部——在上个月于马里兰州帕图森特河海军航空站威廉·A·莫菲特海军上将大楼举行的交接仪式上，海军负责机器人及自主系统事务的直报项目管理者为马修·艾伦上校颁发了新任项目经理聘书。
马里兰州帕图森特河的海军航空系统司令部——负责机器人及自主系统事务的海军直报项目管理者克里斯·米勒主持了此次交接仪式，马修·艾伦在上任后接替了格雷格·斯金纳的职位。斯金纳此前一直领导飞机项目管理办公室，带领该机构在海军及海军陆战队的无人飞行器系统能力发展方面取得了持续进步。
RAS的DRPM克里斯·米勒表示：‘这支团队肩负着重要使命，而格雷格的领导力正是该团队的基石。尽管格雷格一直以极快的速度推动相关能力在海军舰队中的部署，但他同时也打造了一支表现优异、具备强大抗压能力的团队。’
在斯金纳的任职期间，该情报、监视与侦察服务项目累计执行任务飞行时数已超过100万小时，为陆地及海上行动提供了有力支持。自2005年启动以来，该项目已在海军及军事海运司令部的舰船上部署了50多套无人机系统，并在世界各地50多个陆地地点开展作业。
在过去的12个月内，该飞机项目管理办公室还协助完成了4,480架小型无人机系统的交付工作，预计今冬还将有1,520架此类无人机投入使用，以助力实现“无人机优势”战略。该团队推动了海军首个舰载有人与无人协同作战能力的开发，完成了TRV-150C战术补给无人机系统的舰载测试，并为两家供应商颁发了中期空中补给车辆远征后勤相关授权，以便开展下一阶段的无人物流系统原型研发工作。
斯金纳表示：‘指挥权的交接其实是一种传承。我们并非创造了一切，我们所接手的都是前人留下的成果——包括各种组织架构、人际关系、专业知识、传统惯例、宝贵的经验教训以及人们的信任，还有那些在我们到来之前就已为这项任务奉献多年精力的人。’
艾伦是一名经验丰富的海军陆战队军官，曾领导过隶属于步兵部队、航空维护部门、小型战术无人机系统项目以及海岸空中交通管理领域的作战、维护、后勤及采购团队。此前，他曾在总统直升机项目办公室、第29和第31海军陆战队航空后勤中队、第312海军陆战队战斗攻击中队、海岸空中交通管理部门，以及海军部航空/地面事务副助理部长办公室担任领导职务。
2017年至2021年间，艾伦在空军项目管理办公室任职，该办公室前身为海军及海军陆战队小型战术无人机系统项目办公室（PMA 263）。在此期间，他负责推进“无人物流系统-空中版”的快速原型开发工作，并担任RQ-21A“黑杰克”军用无人机的整体产品负责人。他拥有项目管理专业人士认证，同时还具备生命周期物流管理及项目管理方面的高级采购资质。
在讲话中，艾伦回顾了自己重返曾任职机构的经历，并向AIR PMO团队阐述了未来的发展道路。
艾伦表示：“我们将始终把加快系统列装速度作为首要任务。当前形势的紧迫性要求我们必须立即让这些具备模块化设计且具备生存能力的系统投入使用。
海军机器人与自主系统直接汇报项目管理者办公室负责全海军范围内此类系统的研发、需求制定及采购工作。如需了解更多关于该办公室的信息，请访问drpmras.navy.mil。
