items.title: DAF leaders, their spouses highlight families’ role in mission success
items.author: Tech. Sgt. William A. O’Brien
items.summary: During a panel at the 2026 Air, Space & Cyber Conference, senior DAF leaders and their spouses discussed grassroots quality-of-life challenges alongside key initiatives, including the Global Military Spouse Connection pilot, DoD STARBASE STEM programs, and AFPAAS roster integration.
items.body:
Published Oct. 7, 2026

By Tech. Sgt. William A. O’Brien

Secretary of the Air Force Public Affairs

Top Air Force and Space Force leaders, joined by their spouses, offered observations during a panel at the Air, Space and Cyber Conference into the lives of military families and how that dynamic contributes to readiness and defense of the nation.

Luke Air Force Base, Glendale, Arizona

Goodfellow AFB, San Angelo, Texas

Laughlin AFB, Del Rio, Texas

Mountain Home AFB. Mountain Home, Idaho

Travis AFB, Fairfield, California

Patrick Space Force Base, Satellite Beach, Florida

Ramstein AB, Ramstein-Miesenbach

RAF Croughton, United Kingdom

RAF Mildenhall, U.K.

RAF Lakenheath, U.K.

RAF Feltwell, U.K.

Kadena AB, Okinawa, Japan

The program is designed to target military spouse unemployment, which currently has rates around 20%, largely due to frequent permanent change of station moves. GMSC aims to improve career continuity by connecting qualified spouses with DAF civilian employment opportunities before they arrive at their new duty station. “It is a good start,” said CMSAF Wolfe. “With the four spouses here being involved in the [Presidential] Military Spouse Commission, we have an opportunity to make some real change to laws that currently prevent us from hiring people fast enough and putting people in positions and jobs.” STARBASE and STEM Support for Military Children Another family-oriented program mentioned during the panel was STARBASE, a Department of War STEM education program that delivers hands-on, immersive experiences primarily to fifth grade students from military-connected, at-risk and underserved communities. The program seeks to spark interest and inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers and future defense professionals. “Our kids have to live with the decisions of their parents, and I think we owe them the best we possibly can provide,” said CMSAF Wolfe. He stressed the importance of the Air Force investing in educational opportunities for military children, using Starbase as a positive example. The program exposes military youth to the technological environments and positive civilian and military roles found on active, Guard, and Reserve military bases and installations. AFPAAS Card for Spouse Roster Each spouse discussed the challenge in spouse outreach, especially during times when connecting with family is most essential such as deployments and crises. One solution mentioned was an Air Force Personnel Accountability and Assessment System Card , which provides unit leaders with instructional pocket cards and guidance for accessing current personnel and family contact information through the AFPAAS, maintaining accurate recall rosters and securely sharing appropriate roster data with key support liaisons. Improving access to timely contact information, the initiative supports faster outreach to newly arriving spouses and families of deployed Airmen and Guardians, strengthens assistance during permanent change of station moves, deployments, exercises and emergencies and closes gaps in family-support communication. Participation respects privacy, as spouses may opt out of routine contact, while enabling stronger grassroots support networks and unit resilience. Advice to the Next Generation Panelists were asked what advice they would give to young Airmen, Guardians, and their spouses who are just beginning their military journey:

Take every opportunity to grow professionally and personally

Build and nurture strong relationships

Recognize that military service is a family service to the nation

Prioritize physical fitness, financial responsibility and emotional resilience

Understand the “why” behind the mission to support one another more effectively

Never underestimate the power of simple human connection

"You have to really embrace the preciousness of time because you can't get it back,” said CMSSF Bentivegna. “We're always focusing on that next assignment, next rotation, or the next deployment. You think, 'I've got plenty of time to focus on my finances, education, family, relationships … but you can't get that time back. Make the most of it."

items.titleZh: 荷兰国防军高级将领及其配偶强调家庭在任务成功中的重要作用
zhParas: 在2026年航空航天与网络安全会议上的一场小组讨论中，荷兰国防军的高级将领们及其配偶共同探讨了基层官兵生活保障方面面临的种种挑战，同时介绍了多项重要举措，包括“全球军人配偶互助计划”、国防部的STARBASE STEM教育项目，以及将相关人员纳入AFPAAS管理体系的方案。
空军公共事务部长
在2026年空天与网络会议上的一场小组讨论中，空军及太空军的高层领导们与他们的配偶一同参与了讨论，他们分析了军人家庭的生活状况，以及这种家庭环境如何为提升部队的战备状态以及保障国家安全发挥作用。

位于佛罗里达州卫星海滩的帕特里克太空军基地
拉姆施泰因空军基地，拉姆施泰因-米森巴赫
英国克拉夫顿皇家空军基地
位于英国的克拉夫顿皇家空军基地
位于英国的拉克恩希思皇家空军基地

位于日本冲绳的嘉手纳空军基地

该计划旨在解决军人配偶的失业问题，目前这一比例约为20%，其主要原因是部队频繁的永久性驻地调动。GMSC项目旨在在军人配偶抵达新驻地之前，为他们对接DAF的民用就业机会，从而保障其职业发展的连续性。空军参谋长沃尔夫表示：“这是个良好的开端。由于在座的四位配偶都参与了[总统设立的]军人配偶委员会，我们有机会对那些阻碍我们快速招聘人员并为其安排岗位的现行法律进行切实改革。”另一项在研讨会上被提及的以家庭为中心的计划是STARBASE，这是一项由国防部推出的STEM教育项目，主要为来自军人家庭、处于困境或服务不足社区的五年级学生提供沉浸式、实践性的学习体验，旨在激发下一代科学家、工程师及未来国防从业者的兴趣与热情。沃尔夫强调：“我们的孩子不得不承受父母决策带来的影响，我认为我们有责任为他们提供尽可能最好的条件。”他以STARBASE为例，强调了空军为军人子女投资教育资源的重要性——该计划能让这些青少年接触现役部队、国民警卫队及预备役部队基地中的技术环境，以及各类民用和军用岗位。此外，与会配偶还讨论了在人员部署或危机等需要与家人保持联系的关键时刻，开展家属沟通所面临的困难。其中一项解决方案是推出空军人员责任与评估系统卡，这种卡片能为部队领导提供操作指南，帮助他们通过AFPAAS系统获取现有人员及其家属的联系方式，维护准确的名单档案，并安全地与相关支援人员共享必要信息。通过提升及时获取联系信息的能力，该举措有助于更快地与新到任的配偶以及正在执行任务的空军和国民警卫队军人家属取得联系，加强在部队调动、演习及紧急情况下的支援力度，弥补家庭支援沟通中的漏洞。该方案在尊重隐私的前提下运作——配偶可选择不参与常规联系——同时有助于构建更完善的基层支援网络，提升部队的抗风险能力。最后，当被问及会给那些刚刚开始军旅生涯的年轻空军军人、国民警卫队成员及其配偶什么建议时，与会者也给出了自己的意见。
他们充分利用一切机会，在职业素养与个人成长方面不断进步。
他们致力于建立并巩固稳固的亲属关系，强调家庭支持对任务成功的重要作用。
他们认识到，从军其实是一种为国家服务的家庭责任。
他们强调，应优先注重保持良好的身体素质、具备良好的财务责任感以及培养强大的心理韧性。
他们指出，只有深刻理解任务背后的初衷，才能更有效地相互支持，共同应对各种挑战。
千万不要低估简单的人际情感联系所带来的力量。
CMSSF本蒂维尼亚表示：“我们必须真正意识到时间的宝贵，因为它一旦流逝便无法挽回。”她继续说道：“我们总是忙于应对下一项任务、下一次轮岗或下一次部署。人们往往会想‘我有足够的时间来处理财务、学习、家庭事务以及人际关系……’，但那些时间其实是无法再拿回来的。因此应当充分利用好每一分时间。

该计划旨在解决军人配偶的失业问题，目前这一比例约为20%，其主要原因是部队频繁的永久性驻地调动。GMSC项目旨在在军人配偶抵达新驻地之前，为他们对接DAF的民用就业机会，从而保障其职业发展的连续性。空军参谋长沃尔夫表示：“这是个良好的开端。由于在座的四位配偶都参与了[总统设立的]军人配偶委员会，我们有机会对那些阻碍我们快速招聘人员并为其安排岗位的现行法律进行切实改革。”另一项在研讨会上被提及的以家庭为中心的计划是STARBASE，这是一项由国防部推出的STEM教育项目，主要为来自军人家庭、处于困境或服务不足社区的五年级学生提供沉浸式、实践性的学习体验，旨在激发下一代科学家、工程师及未来国防从业者的兴趣与热情。沃尔夫强调：“我们的孩子不得不承受父母决策带来的影响，我认为我们有责任为他们提供尽可能最好的条件。”他以STARBASE为例，强调了空军为军人子女投资教育资源的重要性——该计划能让这些青少年接触现役部队、国民警卫队及预备役部队基地中的技术环境，以及各类民用和军用岗位。此外，与会配偶还讨论了在人员部署或危机等需要与家人保持联系的关键时刻，开展家属沟通所面临的困难。其中一项解决方案是推出空军人员责任与评估系统卡，这种卡片能为部队领导提供操作指南，帮助他们通过AFPAAS系统获取现有人员及其家属的联系方式，维护准确的名单档案，并安全地与相关支援人员共享必要信息。通过提升及时获取联系信息的能力，该举措有助于更快地与新到任的配偶以及正在执行任务的空军和国民警卫队军人家属取得联系，加强在部队调动、演习及紧急情况下的支援力度，弥补家庭支援沟通中的漏洞。该方案在尊重隐私的前提下运作——配偶可选择不参与常规联系——同时有助于构建更完善的基层支援网络，提升部队的抗风险能力。最后，当被问及会给那些刚刚开始军旅生涯的年轻空军军人、国民警卫队成员及其配偶什么建议时，与会者也给出了自己的意见。

他们充分利用一切机会，在职业素养与个人成长方面不断进步。

他们认识到，从军其实是一种为国家服务的家庭责任。

他们强调，应优先注重保持良好的身体素质、具备良好的财务责任感以及培养强大的心理韧性。

他们指出，只有深刻理解任务背后的初衷，才能更有效地相互支持，共同应对各种挑战。

千万不要低估简单的人际情感联系所带来的力量。

CMSSF本蒂维尼亚表示：“我们必须真正意识到时间的宝贵，因为它一旦流逝便无法挽回。”她继续说道：“我们总是忙于应对下一项任务、下一次轮岗或下一次部署。人们往往会想‘我有足够的时间来处理财务、学习、家庭事务以及人际关系……’，但那些时间其实是无法再拿回来的。因此应当充分利用好每一分时间。

items.title: Decades-long mystery solved as lost bomber crew identified
items.summary: The graves of four previously unknown World War 2 Airmen have finally been given names at a ceremony in the Netherlands.
items.body:
Four airmen who died when their Lancaster bomber crashed in Germany in December 1944 were finally honoured by name after an 82-year search uncovered the truth behind one of Bomber Command’s wartime mysteries.

Earlier today at the CWGC ’s Venray War Cemetery in the Netherlands a service was held for Flying Officer ( Fg Off ) Leslie Markland Hough, Royal Australian Air Force ( RAAF ); Pilot Officer ( Plt Off ) John Henry Tales, Royal Air Force Volunteer Reserve ( RAFVR ); Sergeant ( Sgt ) Henry Charles Burnside RAFVR and Sgt John Lawson RAFVR , whose remains lay in graves marked ‘unknown’ for decades following a series of post-war administrative errors.

On the morning of 8 December 1944, the Lancaster PD374 of No. 218 Squadron RAF departed RAF Methwold in Norfolk as part of a force of more than 130 tasked with attacking the Neerbeck oil plant at Homberg in Germany’s Ruhr region. From the seven man Lancaster crew; three escaped by parachute and were taken as Prisoners of War and the other four lost their lives.

JCCC Caseworker, Tracey Bowers, said:

Today we honour the British and Australian airmen who served and died together during World War 2. To have so many families present here today has made this occasion especially poignant, and seeing them interacting with members of the local community who have adopted these graves incredibly moving.

Plt Off Tales, born in Attercliffe, Sheffield, on 31 December 1917 was one of eleven children. He worked as a poster writer before enlisting in the RAF in September 1939 where he built an exemplary service record. Despite having already completed a full operational tour, he volunteered to return to frontline operations and joined No. 218 Squadron in August 1944.

John Tales, nephew of Plt Off Tales, who attended the service with other family members said:

It has been an extremely poignant occasion and we are honoured and quite overwhelmed to have been here. It has been wonderful to learn more about our Uncle John and we would like to thank all those who have made this possible

The Captain of Lancaster PD374 was Australian airman Fg Off Hough RAAF . Eyewitness accounts suggest Hough remained at the controls of the burning aircraft to give others the opportunity to escape.

The two other crew honoured were Sgts Burnside and Lawson. Burnside was known for his professionalism and immaculate appearance, while Lawson, affectionately known as “Geordie”, came from a mining family in County Durham.

Thurston Lawson, nephew of Sgt Lawson who attended the service with his cousin John Lawson said:

Fantastic day and incredibly memorable. So moving to see so many people here and everyone has been so kind and represented their organisations brilliantly.

The rededication service was conducted by Reverend (Group Captain) Ruth Hake, who said:

It is my immense privilege to conduct the ceremony for Fg Off Hough, Plt Off Tales, Sgt Burnside and Sgt Lawson today. They gave their lives in defence of our nation, and in dedicating their graves today with their names rightfully in place, we are able finally, to honour that debt that we all owe to them and their loved ones.

Today’s service, held more than eight decades after these men lost their lives, means the crew of Lancaster PD374 will finally be commemorated under their own names rather than as unknown servicemen.

Dr Daniel Seaton, Commemorations Case Officer at the CWGC , said:

I am delighted that, after so many years, the final resting place of these brave airmen has finally been identified. Their family members, of whom so many were here today, can now visit their known graves in perpetuity. The Commission is pleased to have assisted with this process and will continue to maintain their graves with the utmost care and respect.

items.titleZh: 历经数十年之谜终得破解，失事轰炸机机组人员身份得以确认
zhParas: 1944年12月，一架兰开斯特轰炸机在德国坠毁，导致四名飞行员丧生。经过82年的调查终于揭开了轰炸机司令部在二战期间留下的谜团真相，这四名飞行员的姓名也终于在荷兰举行的一场仪式上被正式公布，得以得到应有的纪念。
今天早些时候，在荷兰的CWGC芬雷战争公墓举行了一场纪念仪式，悼念澳大利亚皇家空军的中尉莱斯利·马克兰德·霍夫、英国皇家空军志愿预备队的飞行员约翰·亨利·泰尔斯，以及同样属于英国皇家空军志愿预备队的亨利·查尔斯·伯恩赛德中士和约翰·劳森中士。由于战后一系列行政失误，这四名军人的遗体数十年间都被标记为“身份不明”，如今终于在仪式上被正式确认身份并得到应有的纪念。
1944年12月8日上午，英国皇家空军第218中队的兰开斯特轰炸机PD374号从诺福克的梅斯沃尔德机场起飞，参与了这支由130多架飞机组成的联军行动，共同目标是袭击位于德国鲁尔区的霍姆贝格地区的尼尔贝克石油厂。在这架兰开斯特轰炸机的七名机组人员中，有三人通过跳伞逃生并成为战俘，而其余四人则不幸遇难。
JCCC案件处理员特蕾西·鲍尔斯表示：
今天，我们向在第二次世界大战期间一同服役并牺牲的英国与澳大利亚飞行员致以敬意。众多家属齐聚于此，让这一时刻更具意义；而看到他们与那些照料这些墓地的当地居民互动的场景，更是令人动容至极。
1917年12月31日，泰尔斯中尉出生于谢菲尔德的阿特克利夫，是家中的11个孩子之一。在1939年9月加入英国皇家空军之前，他一直从事海报设计工作，入伍后则展现出极为出色的服役表现。尽管已经完成了一次完整的作战任务，他仍主动请求重返前线，于1944年8月加入了第218中队。
参加仪式的其他家属中，有泰尔斯中尉的侄子约翰·泰尔斯，他说道：
这真是一个极其令人感动的时刻，能来到这里我们感到无比荣幸，同时也有些不知所措。能够进一步了解我们的约翰叔叔，实在是一件美好的事，我们想感谢所有为促成这一时刻而付出努力的人。
兰开斯特PD374飞机的机长是澳大利亚皇家空军中尉霍夫，他为了给其他机组人员争取逃生机会，始终坚守在正在燃烧的飞机操控舱内。
另一位获追授荣誉的机组人员是伯恩赛德中士和劳森中士。伯恩赛德以专业素养和一丝不苟的仪容著称，而被称为“乔迪”的劳森则出身于达勒姆郡的一个矿工家庭。
与表兄约翰·劳森一同出席仪式的劳森中士的侄子瑟斯顿·劳森表示：
真是美好又令人难以忘怀的一天。能见到这么多人在场，实在令人感动，而且每个人都十分友善，还将各自所属的机构代表得极为出色。
此次重祭仪式由鲁思·黑克牧师（集团上校军衔）主持，她在仪式上表示：
今天能够为霍夫中尉、泰尔斯少尉、伯恩赛德中士以及劳森中士主持这场纪念仪式，我深感荣幸。这四位军人为了保卫我们的国家献出了生命，而通过今日为他们的坟墓刻上姓名，我们终于能够履行对她们以及她们的亲友所欠下的那份责任，向她们致以应有的敬意。
在這些軍人牺牲八十余年之後，今天的紀念儀式終於讓蘭开斯特PD374號飛機的乘員們能夠以真實姓名被銘記，而不再只是作為身份不明的戰士被記載在歷史中。
英国战争纪念公署的纪念事务负责人丹尼尔·西顿博士表示：
我很高兴，经过这么多年的追寻，这些英勇飞行员的长眠之地终于被确定下来。今天在场的许多飞行员家属如今可以永远前往他们已找到位置的墓地祭扫了。该委员会为推动这一进程感到欣慰，并将继续以最谨慎的态度和最高的敬意维护他们的墓地。

items.title: MSC Bids Farewell to Force Master Chief Steven Bosco After 33 Years of Service
items.author: Molly Burgess
items.summary: NORFOLK, Va.- Military Sealift Command (MSC) bid farewell to Force Master Chief Steven Bosco, MSC Command Master Chief, as he closed the last chapter of 33 years of naval service during a retirement ceremony at Vista Point Center, onboard Naval Station Norfolk, Norfolk, Va., Oct. 2, 2026.
items.body:
NORFOLK, Va.- Military Sealift Command (MSC) bid farewell to Force Master Chief Steven Bosco, MSC Command Master Chief, as he closed the last chapter of 33 years of naval service during a retirement ceremony at Vista Point Center, onboard Naval Station Norfolk, Norfolk, Va., Oct. 2, 2026.

Bosco was surrounded by friends, family, and shipmates to honor his service and listen to the stories and memories from past leaders who served alongside him during his naval career.

“Steve is a phenomenal person,” Rear Adm. Benjamin Nicholson, Commander, Military Sealift Command, said during his opening speech as the ceremony’s presiding officer. “When it comes to caring about others, Steve is the type of person who learns everything there is to know about everyone he possibly can.”

Retired Vice Adm. James Pitts was a guest speaker for the event and highlighted Bosco’s career successes and his achievement of rising through the naval ranks to force master chief.

“In 27 years, he rose from a brand-new recruit to be the top enlisted advisor to the commander of the submarine force and the entire submarine force leadership,” Pitts said. “When you look at any given year, the Navy brings in about 40,000 new Sailors, and so the odds that a single Sailor who comes in becomes a force master chief is roughly 0.01%. That’s one out of every 10,000.”

During the ceremony, guest speaker retired Rear Adm. Philip Sobeck, MSC’s commander prior to retiring, spoke of the dedication Bosco had for his work, his Sailors, the command, and how he became a pillar in Sobeck’s life.

“When I say I am a Steve Bosco trained Sailor, it means in the way of understanding at a deckplate level, of being seen without being seen, and ensuring that those in power are actually making a difference and being held accountable,” Sobeck said. “He absolutely saved my life, and when you make that much of an impact on someone, it says a lot about your humanity, and you as an individual.”

Taking the microphone for his final remarks, Bosco thanked those in attendance and reflected on the opportunities the Navy afforded him as well as the deep professional bonds he forged within the chiefs’ mess.

“For someone who has worn anchors for 24 of my 33 years, my true naval anchor will always be the chiefs’ mess,” said Bosco. “The mess, both past and present, you are the backbone of every solution, you are the keepers of tradition, and you are the drivers of the mission.”

Bosco went on to share his gratitude for the unwavering support from his family over the years.

“When I say personal support, that starts and ends with my family. My family is my anchor, my bedrock and everything in between,” Bosco said. “My wife, my kids and my extended family, thank you for your unconditional love, your patience and keeping me grounded for 33 years of service. This milestone belongs to you, as much as it does to me.”

Before Bosco took his final walk down the red carpet lined with sideboys and chiefs from the past and the present to retire himself and his family, Pitts expanded on Bosco’s legacy as a leader and the impact he leaves following his retirement.

“When Steve made chief, senior chief and master chief, Sailors all over the world were cheering because they knew the right person had been selected,” Pitts said. “The legacy that Steve leaves you in his retirement and for the foreseeable future, Sailors all over the world now will proudly claim ‘I was Steve Bosco trained’.”

MSC exists to support the joint warfighter across the full spectrum of military operations, with a workforce that includes approximately 6,000 Civil Service Mariners and 1,500 contract mariners, supported by 1,500 shore staff and 3,500 active duty and reserve military personnel.

美军海运司令部司令本杰明·尼科尔森海军少将在担任仪式主持人的开场致辞中表示：‘史蒂文是个极其出色的人。在关心他人方面，他总是竭尽所能去了解每一个他能够接触的人。’
作为特邀演讲人出席此次活动的退役海军少将詹姆斯·皮茨，重点介绍了博斯科在职业生涯中所取得的优异成绩，以及他如何一步步晋升，最终成为海军最高级别的军士长。
皮茨表示，博斯科在27年的军旅生涯中从一名新兵一步步晋升，最终成为潜艇部队指挥官及整个潜艇部队领导层的最高级别士官顾问。他进一步指出，海军每年都会招募约4万名新水兵，而其中能晋升为部队士官长的概率仅有0.01%，也就是说每1万人中才有一人能达到这一地位。
在最后的致辞中，史蒂文·博斯科握着麦克风向在场的所有人表示感谢，他回顾了海军给予自己的成长机会，以及自己在海军军官群体中建立的深厚职业情谊。
博斯科表示：“在33年的海军服役生涯中，有24年我都身着海军制服，而对我而言，真正的‘海军支柱’永远是士官食堂。无论是过去的还是现在的那些士官们，你们都是各项任务得以完成的坚强后盾，是传统的守护者，也是推动任务前进的驱动力。
博斯科接着表达了对家人多年来给予他坚定支持的感激之情。
博斯科说道：‘当我谈到个人支持时，其起点与终点都是我的家人。我的家人是我前进的支柱、最坚实的后盾，更是支撑我一切的力量。’他继续表示：‘我的妻子、孩子们以及整个大家庭，感谢你们33年来无条件的爱、耐心，以及始终让我保持冷静与坚定的支持。这一重要时刻既属于我，也同样属于你们。’
在博斯科在由历任及现任高级军官陪同、走过铺满红毯的通道、与家人一同步入退休生活之前，皮茨进一步阐述了博斯科作为领导者的卓越贡献，以及他离任后仍会产生的深远影响。
皮茨表示：“当史蒂夫先后晋升为高级军士、军士长以及军士长级指挥官时，全世界的海军士兵们都为之欢欣，因为他们知道最合适的人选已被选中。在结束33年的海军服役生涯并退休之后，史蒂夫仍会留下宝贵的精神遗产，让全世界的海军士兵都能自豪地宣称‘我曾接受过史蒂夫·博斯科的训练’。
军事海运司令部旨在为各类军事行动中的联合作战人员提供全方位支持，其队伍由约6,000名文职海员和1,500名合同制海员组成，同时还得到1,500名岸基工作人员以及3,500名现役及预备役军人的协助。

items.title: USACE, Port Tampa Bay agreement strengthens permitting coordination
items.author: Peggy Bebb
items.summary: TAMPA, Fla. - The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Jacksonville District, and Port Tampa Bay have formalized a partnership intended to support timely, transparent review of the port’s Department of the Army permit applications while maintaining the independent environmental and public-interest safeguards required by federal law.
items.body:
TAMPA, Fla. - The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Jacksonville District, and Port Tampa Bay have formalized a partnership intended to support timely, transparent review of the port’s Department of the Army permit applications while maintaining the independent environmental and public-interest safeguards required by federal law.

The agreement, authorized under Section 214 of the Water Resources Development Act (WRDA), allows eligible non-federal public entities to contribute funds to USACE to evaluate their permit applications. In this case, Port Tampa Bay will fund a designated portion of a Jacksonville District Regulatory Project Manager’s time to support the port’s regulatory workload.

For a port with numerous large, connected projects underway or planned, the agreement provides a consistent point of contact and a structured way to manage technical reviews, information exchanges and evolving project priorities.

“Port Tampa Bay has a high volume of complex work requiring extensive regulatory oversight,” Jacksonville District’s Tampa Regulatory Section Chief, Mindy Hogan-Charles said. “This agreement establishes a direct partnership that supports clear communication, reliable tracking and dedicated review hours, without diverting essential regulatory resources from other applicants in the Tampa area.”

Port Tampa Bay is Florida’s largest port by cargo tonnage and land area. Its infrastructure needs can include berth modifications and expansions, maintenance dredging, channel deepening and preservation work on dredged-material management-area islands. Because these initiatives are often large-scale, multi-phase projects, they frequently require individual Department of the Army permit reviews rather than simpler general-permit verifications. Some actions also require coordination or formal consultation with other federal agencies.

Under the agreement, a designated Regulatory Project Manager will serve as the primary conduit between Jacksonville District’s Regulatory Division and Port Tampa Bay. The manager will devote a defined portion of each workweek to port actions, with the remainder of the workweek supporting review of non-port permit applications within the broader Tampa Area of Responsibility.

That split schedule is central to the agreement’s public benefit. It gives the port dedicated, predictable support for its permit applications while keeping the regulatory professional actively engaged in work affecting other applicants in Pinellas and Hillsborough counties. The arrangement also helps the Tampa permits section manage overall workload and strengthens its capacity to serve local, state and federal agencies, homeowners, environmental consultants and commercial developers.

Rachel Somerville, who has served as the port’s primary Regulatory Project Manager during the past year and a half, will continue in the dedicated role. Her existing familiarity with the port’s regulatory actions, project history and technical background will help sustain continuity as the agreement moves forward.

“Having one reliable project manager creates stability for everyone involved,” Somerville said. “The port knows who to contact, and USACE has a clear view of how multiple port projects relate to one another. That helps us maintain consistent communication, track timelines and focus review efforts where they are needed most.” A single point of contact is especially valuable because port projects often overlap in location, timing and environmental considerations. A dedicated project manager can retain institutional knowledge from one project to the next, better understand how proposed activities interact and coordinate internally with USACE Civil Works staff when port work intersects with federally maintained navigation projects in Tampa Bay.

The agreement also establishes regular coordination practices, including dedicated weekly project-evaluation time and recurring monthly meetings. These touchpoints are intended to help USACE and Port Tampa Bay identify issues early, clarify application needs and align regulatory reviews with the port’s changing construction and operational priorities.

Importantly, the agreement does not give Port Tampa Bay preferential treatment or alter any environmental standard. The funds contributed pay only for the time spent reviewing applications; they do not determine a permit decision. USACE retains full authority to approve, deny or modify every Department of the Army permit application based on applicable laws, environmental analysis and the public-interest review process.

All port projects will continue to comply with applicable federal requirements, including the Clean Water Act, Rivers and Harbors Act, National Environmental Policy Act, National Historic Preservation Act and Endangered Species Act.

To preserve the integrity and independence of the permitting process, Somerville’s work as the project manager is subject to a second level of oversight. The Tampa Section Chief will review final documents before they are provided to the port. Compliance and enforcement actions, if necessary, will be handled by an impartial USACE employee who is not funded by the port.

“This agreement supports timeliness, but it does not change the standard for a permit decision,” Hogan-Charles said. “USACE’s responsibility remains the same: evaluate every action objectively and protect aquatic resources” The agreement’s development began in 2016 and required sustained coordination between the Jacksonville District and Port Tampa Bay. The partners worked through changes in national WRDA legislation, carefully defined a split-work schedule that complied with federal labor requirements and established professional safeguards to prevent outside funding from influencing regulatory decisions. The new agreement will remain in effect for three years and can be extended.

Those efforts were grounded in transparency, frequent communication and a shared objective: create a more efficient process for complex port infrastructure work without compromising fairness for other permit applicants or the integrity of USACE’s regulatory program.

Success will be measured in several ways. For the Jacksonville District, the agreement is expected to help reduce permitting processing times in the Tampa Area of Responsibility and allow resources to be directed toward other large, complex projects outside the port’s boundaries. For Port Tampa Bay, success means greater predictability in meeting planning and construction milestones.

One example of how this partnership supports these goals is the proposed 10-year maintenance dredging permit currently being finalized by USACE. Compared with a five-year permit, this longer authorization would reduce the frequency of permit renewals and give the port more flexibility to schedule dredging as needed to maintain safe access to its channels and berths at previously authorized depths. This approach supports coordinated, long-term planning between USACE and the port while allowing USACE staff to focus on other priority projects.

For the public, the intended benefits include reliable port operations that support regional economic growth and jobs, alongside continued protection of Tampa Bay’s aquatic resources. Required safeguards would include seasonal restrictions to protect Florida manatees, barriers to limit the spread of sediment and protect water quality, and practices that protect and restore migratory shorebird habitat on islands used for dredged material placement.

The agreement may also offer a model for future partnerships with other eligible public infrastructure entities in Florida. By using a partial-position structure, USACE can expand specialized regulatory capacity while continuing to serve the broader community and preserve local expertise.

Ultimately, the USACE and Port Tampa Bay agreement is designed to demonstrate that efficient permitting coordination and independent environmental stewardship can advance together: improving predictability for critical infrastructure projects, supporting the regional supply chain and ensuring that every permit decision remains grounded in federal law and the public interest.
items.summaryZh: 佛罗里达州坦帕市——美国陆军工程兵团杰克逊维尔分局与坦帕湾港口已正式建立合作伙伴关系，旨在在确保及时、透明地审查该港口提交的陆军相关许可申请的同时，遵循联邦法律要求，维持独立的环保与公共利益保障机制。
items.titleZh: 美国陆军工程兵团与坦帕湾港口达成协议，强化许可审批协作
zhParas: 佛罗里达州坦帕市——美国陆军工程兵团杰克逊维尔分局与坦帕湾港口已正式建立合作伙伴关系，旨在在确保及时、透明地审查该港口提交的陆军相关许可申请的同时，遵循联邦法律要求，维持独立的环保与公共利益保障机制。
根据《水资源开发法》第214条的规定，该协议允许符合条件的非联邦公共机构为美国陆军工程兵团提供资金，用于协助其审查相关许可申请。在此次合作中，坦帕湾港口将出资支持杰克逊维尔分局的监管项目负责人投入部分工作时间，以帮助港口处理日益繁重的监管工作。
对于那些正在实施或计划开展众多大型关联项目的港口而言，该协议确立了统一的联络窗口，并通过系统化的机制来处理技术审查、信息交流以及不断变化的项目优先级问题。
坦帕湾港是佛罗里达州按货物吞吐量和陆地面积计算最大的港口。该港口的基础设施建设需求可能包括泊位改造与扩建、维护性疏浚、航道加深，以及疏浚产生的淤泥处理相关工作。由于这些项目往往规模庞大且分多个阶段实施，因此通常需要由陆军部逐一进行审批，而非简单的统一许可核查；部分工程还须与其他联邦机构协调或进行正式磋商。
根据该协议，一名指定的监管项目经理将担任杰克逊维尔分区的监管部门与坦帕湾港之间的主要联络人。这名项目经理每周会安排固定时间处理与港口相关的事务，其余时间则负责审查坦帕责任区域内的其他非港口类许可申请。
这种分阶段的工作安排正是该协议能带来公共利益的关键所在。它既为坦帕湾港的许可申请提供了专门且可预测的支持，又能确保负责监管工作的专业人员持续处理皮内拉斯县和希尔斯伯勒县其他申请人的相关事务。此外，这种安排还有助于坦帕港的许可审批部门更好地管理整体工作量，进而提升其为当地政府机构、州级及联邦政府部门、房主、环境咨询机构以及商业开发商提供服务的能力。
在过去一年半的时间里一直担任坦帕湾港主要监管项目经理的雷切尔·萨默维尔将继续承担这一职责。由于她早已熟悉该港口的监管流程、项目历史及技术背景，因此在协议持续实施的过程中，她将有助于确保各项工作的连贯性。
该协议还确立了定期的协调机制，包括每周专门用于项目评估的时间以及每月召开的例会。通过这些沟通渠道，美国陆军工程兵团杰克逊维尔分局与坦帕湾港口能够及早发现存在的问题，明确申请方的需求，并使监管审查工作与港口不断变化的建设及运营重点保持一致。
重要的是，该协议并未给予坦帕湾港口任何优先待遇，也不会改变任何环境标准。所提供的资金仅用于支付审核申请所耗费的时间，不会影响许可审批的结果。美国陆军工程兵团仍拥有完全的权力，可依据相关法律法规、环境评估结果以及公众利益考量，对每一份陆军部的许可申请进行批准、拒绝或修改。
所有港口项目仍需遵守相关的联邦法规要求，其中包括《清洁水法》、《河流与港口法》、《国家环境政策法》、《国家历史保护法》以及《濒危物种法》。
为确保许可审批流程的公正性与独立性，担任该项目经理的萨默维尔的工作还需接受另一层监督。坦帕分部的负责人会在相关文件提交给港口之前对其进行审核；如有必要采取合规监管措施，则由一名不从港口获得经费支持、立场公正的美国陆军工程兵团员工来处理。
这些举措建立在透明度、频繁沟通以及共同目标的基础之上，即在不损害其他申请人的公平权益或美国陆军工程兵团监管体系的公正性的前提下，为复杂的港口基础设施建设打造更高效的审批流程。
该协议的成效将通过多项指标来衡量。对于杰克逊维尔分局而言，这一合作有望缩短坦帕责任区域内的审批流程时间，从而将更多资源投入到港口周边其他规模庞大、结构复杂的项目中。而对坦帕湾港口而言，其成功则体现在能够更精准地把握规划与建设各阶段的节点时间。
该合作伙伴关系助力实现上述目标的其中一个实例，便是目前由美国陆军工程兵团正在最终敲定的为期10年的港口维护疏浚许可。相较于5年的许可期限，更长的授权时间不仅能减少许可续期的频率，还能让港口更灵活地安排疏浚工作，从而始终将航道与泊位维持在既定深度，确保航行安全。这一举措既促进了美国陆军工程兵团与港口之间的协同长期规划，也能让工程兵团的工作人员将精力集中在其他优先项目中。
对公众而言，这一合作带来的益处包括保障港口的稳定运营，从而推动区域经济发展并创造就业机会，同时也有助于持续保护坦帕湾的水生资源。为确保这些目标得以实现，相关措施将包括设定季节性限制以保护佛罗里达海牛，设置屏障防止沉积物扩散以维护水质，以及采取相应措施保护和恢复用于堆放疏浚物的岛屿上的候鸟栖息地。
总体而言，美国陆军工程兵团杰克逊维尔分局与坦帕湾港口达成的这项协议旨在证明，高效的许可审批协调与独立的环保监管是完全可以并行推进的：它既能提升关键基础设施项目的可预见性，为区域供应链提供保障，也能确保每一项许可决策都符合联邦法律要求并兼顾公共利益。

items.title: New course empowers safety officers, enlisted to reduce preventable mishaps
items.author: Charity Robinson
items.summary: Navy officers and enlisted Sailors leading and assigned to safety departments will soon have the opportunity to gain the knowledge and tools to promote effective risk management principles within their organizations to help reduce preventable mishaps.
items.body:
NORFOLK, Va. – Navy officers and enlisted Sailors leading and assigned to safety departments will soon have the opportunity to gain the knowledge and tools to promote effective risk management principles within their organizations to help reduce preventable mishaps.

The Naval School of Aviation Safety (SAS) in Pensacola, Florida, is launching its new Risk Management Safety Officer (RMSO) course in late 2026. The first course will run Dec. 1-11 and is intended for Navy and Marine Corps officers in grades O-3 to O-5, as well as senior enlisted Sailors and Marines in grades E-6 to E-8. While open to qualified personnel, attendance is strongly encouraged by safety office department heads due to the advanced nature of the curriculum.

SAS falls under the oversight of Commander, Naval Safety Command in Norfolk, Virginia. Although the course was designed initially in response to a Marine Corps request, Navy Capt. Daniel Testa, SAS commanding officer, said the Navy will also find value in the course. “Upon completion of this first course, we will deliver professional Navy and Marine Corps safety managers with an in-depth understanding of risk management,” said Testa. “The RMSO course will continue to evolve to align with emerging hazards and operational lessons learned in response to student feedback.”

The initial course offering will include 50 Marine Corps quotas and between six and eight slots for Navy personnel. Beginning in FY28, the course will expand with the hiring of additional RMSO instructors and will be offered up to seven times a year to provide more seats for Navy personnel.

“The Marine Corps identified a need within the non-aviation communities to create a safety and standardization office and instill a more robust culture of risk management and safety. To speed up the institution of this new initiative, the Marine Corps is drawing from the aviation community’s lessons learned over the past 50 years,” said Maj. Bryan Leicht, SAS instructor. “Pulling concepts from the SAS Aviation Safety Officer (ASO) course, we’ve adapted the courseware to be applicable for the entire Naval enterprise to support other warfare communities and our combat arms brethren within the Navy and Marine Corps.”

Concepts from the ASO course were adapted, structured and broken down into the following core areas: Crew/Team Resource Management, Safety Management System, Investigations, Reporting and Medical/Human Factors. According to Leicht, an in-residence course will be the only option – at least for the time being, due to the nature of the curriculum which will consist of running mishap drills, performing hands-on investigations at the schoolhouse’s crash lab and executing practical exercises. He also noted that SAS executes a hotwash after each course where critiques have been submitted to discuss lessons learned, new information from Safety Investigation Reports (SIRs) or fleet feedback, enabling the schoolhouse to remain flexible enough to adjust the curriculum.

“One of the great things about owning our curriculum is that we can be very adaptable and flexible,” said Testa. “If a gap is identified in the fleet, one of the first places they will typically contact is the schoolhouse to see if we are teaching [a course] to address that gap. If not, we can easily build it into our curriculum.”

SAS courses are designed to be responsive to the evolving operational environment, an important resource that reflects the CNO’s priority of continually improving the naval service’s wartime advantage while building a more adaptive and decisive maritime force.

“During a recent safety summit, the question came up of how we can prevent aviation ground mishaps,” said Leicht. “This course seeks to prepares RMSOs to implement an integrated safety management system throughout the unit. Additionally, it equips them with the tools necessary to better identify risks and implement appropriate controls, mitigating most issues before they happen. Having the right people – a quality assurance officer or quality assurance chief with the understanding of how to incorporate risk and how to integrate that with the safety office, is a potential benefit out there to reduce mishaps.

“We want to teach the critical thinking aspect of being able to observe, analyze risk and communicate that risk to the commander so they can make informed decisions,” he added. “Proper identification and mitigation of risk allows us to operate more aggressively in a warfighting environment.”

Ultimately, Leicht said the school wants to ensure Sailors and Marines are making informed risk decisions and implementing a good risk control system that fosters a good risk management culture.

For more information, Marines can sign up through the following link (mailto:USMC%20RMSO%20Sign%20up) and email the form to Maj Calloway (mailto:Ronald.calloway@usmc.mil) at RMD per MARDMIN 456/26 .

Navy personnel can email Capt. Leicht (mailto:bryan.t.leicht.mil@us.navy.mil) directly with their request to this email.
items.summaryZh: 弗吉尼亚州诺福克——负责领导或承担安全管理任务的海军军官及士兵们，即将有机会掌握相关的知识与方法，从而在所属单位中更好地实施有效的风险管理措施，进而减少那些本可避免的事故。
items.titleZh: 新课程助力海军安全官员与士兵提升能力，以减少可避免的事故
zhParas: 弗吉尼亚州诺福克——负责领导或承担安全管理任务的海军军官及士兵们，即将有机会掌握相关的知识与方法，从而在所属单位中更好地实施有效的风险管理措施，进而减少那些本可避免的事故。
位于佛罗里达州彭萨科拉的海军航空安全学校将于2026年底开设新的风险管理安全官课程。首期课程将于12月1日至11日举办，面向军衔为O-3至O-5级的海军及海军陆战队军官，以及军衔为E-6至E-8级的高级士兵和海军陆战队员。尽管该课程对符合条件的人员开放，但由于其内容较为深入，各安全管理部门的负责人仍强烈建议相关人员参加学习。
位于弗吉尼亚州诺福克的海军安全司令部负责监管SAS项目。尽管该课程最初是应海军陆战队的要求而设计的，但SAS的指挥官、海军上尉丹尼尔·特斯塔表示，海军同样能从这门课程中获益。特斯塔称：‘完成首期课程后，我们将培养出具备深入风险管理知识的专业海军及海军陆战队安全管理人员。’此外，该课程还将根据学员反馈以及新出现的危险形势和作战经验不断进行调整完善。
首批开设的课程将为海军陆战队预留50个名额，同时为海军人员提供6至8个学习机会。从2028财年起，随着更多RMSO培训讲师的加入，该课程的开设频率将提高，每年最多可举办7期，以便为更多海军人员提供学习机会。
海军陆战队意识到非航空领域的部队也需要设立专门的安全部门与标准化机构，以建立更为完善的危机管理与安全文化。SAS教官布赖恩·莱希特少校表示，为加快这一新举措的推行，海军陆战队借鉴了航空领域50年来积累的经验教训；通过吸收SAS航空安全官课程中的相关理念，他们对课程内容进行了调整，使其能够适用于整个海军体系，从而为海军及其他军种的作战部队提供支持。

ASO课程中的相关理念经过调整与梳理，被划分为以下核心模块：机组/团队资源管理、安全管理体制、事故调查、报告撰写以及军事/人为因素分析。莱希特表示，鉴于该课程的内容包括组织事故演练、在学校的碰撞实验室进行实际调查以及开展各类实践训练，至少在目前阶段，只能以面授课程的形式开展教学。他还提到，SAS会在每期课程结束后组织总结会议，针对收到的反馈意见、安全调查报告中的新信息以及舰队方面的建议进行讨论，从而让课程体系能够保持灵活性，及时作出调整。
泰斯塔表示：‘拥有自主设计的课程最大的优势就在于其极高的适应性与灵活性。’他进一步说明，‘一旦舰队中发现某些能力缺口，他们通常首先会联系培训学院，看我们是否有相关课程可用于弥补这一缺口；如果没有，我们也能轻松将其纳入课程体系之中。’
这些特种作战课程的设置旨在及时应对不断变化的作战环境，这一重要举措体现了海军部长致力于持续提升海军在战争中的优势，同时打造一支更具适应能力与决策力的海上作战力量这一战略目标。
他补充道：‘我们希望让安全官员和士兵掌握关键思维能力，学会观察、分析风险，并将这些风险信息及时传达给指挥官，以便其做出明智决策。’他进一步指出，‘只有准确识别并有效降低风险，我们才能在作战环境中更积极地展开行动。’
莱希特表示，该培训项目旨在确保海军水兵和海军陆战队士兵能够基于充分信息作出风险决策，同时建立完善的控制体系，进而培育良好的风险管理体系文化。
根据MARDMIN 456/26的相关规定，海军陆战队人员如需了解更多信息，可通过以下链接（mailto:USMC%20RMSO%20Sign%20up）填写表格，然后发送至RMD部门的Calloway少校邮箱（mailto:Ronald.calloway@usmc.mil）即可。
海军官兵若有意参加该培训，可直接将申请邮件发送至Leicht上尉的邮箱（mailto:bryan.t.leicht.mil@us.navy.mil）进行咨询。

ASO课程中的相关理念经过调整与梳理，被划分为以下核心模块：机组/团队资源管理、安全管理体制、事故调查、报告撰写以及军事/人为因素分析。莱希特表示，鉴于该课程的内容包括组织事故演练、在学校的碰撞实验室进行实际调查以及开展各类实践训练，至少在目前阶段，只能以面授课程的形式开展教学。他还提到，SAS会在每期课程结束后组织总结会议，针对收到的反馈意见、安全调查报告中的新信息以及舰队方面的建议进行讨论，从而让课程体系能够保持灵活性，及时作出调整。

泰斯塔表示：‘拥有自主设计的课程最大的优势就在于其极高的适应性与灵活性。’他进一步说明，‘一旦舰队中发现某些能力缺口，他们通常首先会联系培训学院，看我们是否有相关课程可用于弥补这一缺口；如果没有，我们也能轻松将其纳入课程体系之中。’

这些特种作战课程的设置旨在及时应对不断变化的作战环境，这一重要举措体现了海军部长致力于持续提升海军在战争中的优势，同时打造一支更具适应能力与决策力的海上作战力量这一战略目标。



他补充道：‘我们希望让安全官员和士兵掌握关键思维能力，学会观察、分析风险，并将这些风险信息及时传达给指挥官，以便其做出明智决策。’他进一步指出，‘只有准确识别并有效降低风险，我们才能在作战环境中更积极地展开行动。’

莱希特表示，该培训项目旨在确保海军水兵和海军陆战队士兵能够基于充分信息作出风险决策，同时建立完善的控制体系，进而培育良好的风险管理体系文化。

根据MARDMIN 456/26的相关规定，海军陆战队人员如需了解更多信息，可通过以下链接（mailto:USMC%20RMSO%20Sign%20up）填写表格，然后发送至RMD部门的Calloway少校邮箱（mailto:Ronald.calloway@usmc.mil）即可。

海军官兵若有意参加该培训，可直接将申请邮件发送至Leicht上尉的邮箱（mailto:bryan.t.leicht.mil@us.navy.mil）进行咨询。

items.title: Embraer, Lockheed Martin vie for India’s $10.5B military transport aircraft deal
items.author: Anjana Pasricha
items.summary: The Indian government wants one of its biggest military aviation contracts to deepen the country’s local aerospace industrial base.
items.body:
NEW DELHI — Global aerospace companies Embraer from Brazil and Lockheed Martin from the United States are offering to expand aircraft manufacturing facilities in India as they pursue an approximately $10.5 billion contract for 60 medium transport aircraft for the Indian Air Force.

Embraer’s C-390 Millennium is competing with Lockheed Martin’s C-130J Super Hercules as India seeks to replace its aging military transport fleet that includes the Soviet-era Antonov An-32.

The formal race for one of India’s biggest military aviation contracts set off in August when India issued a Request for Proposal to five Indian companies setting the stage for the bidding. Global aviation companies are partnering with Indian firms because New Delhi has mandated that while the initial multi role aircraft will be delivered ready to fly, the rest must be built domestically.

With India’s focus on building a local aerospace industrial base, Embraer announced on Oct. 1 that the company and its Indian partner, Mahindra Defence, have identified the central Indian city of Nagpur as a production site for the aircraft if they are awarded the contract.

“Identifying Nagpur as a potential location for an assembly facility is an important step in building a robust, long-term aerospace ecosystem in the country,” said Bosco da Costa Junior, president and CEO of Embraer Defense & Security, in a joint statement with Mahindra.

The two companies said they will progressively integrate Indian aerospace companies into the C-390 Millennium ecosystem to deliver manufacturing, training and lifecycle support.

Lockheed Martin already has a presence in India — the Indian Air Force currently operates 12 C-130J Super Hercules aircraft. The company says the aircraft it is now offering, the C-130J-30 in its Block 8.1.2 configuration, will be more advanced than the ones currently with the air force.

If it wins, Lockheed has said that 12 aircraft would be built in the U.S. and 48 in India in partnership with Tata Advanced Systems Limited, with which it has a joint venture.

The American company already has a manufacturing base in India. It makes key components, including the aircraft’s empennage or tail assembly, locally with Tata.

Winning the contract would mean establishing a bigger industrial footprint in India, Dan Tenney, Lockheed Martin’s senior vice president for global business development and strategy, recently told the Press Trust of India.

“We have a long partnership with Tata that produces components and empennages of the C-130J aircraft. It is a very robust capability that will be expanded in our current bid,” he said.

The company has also proposed upgrading the Indian Air Force’s existing fleet of 12 C-130Js.

India has set a requirement of minimum 40% domestic content for the aircraft. Because the country shares long Himalayan borders with rivals Pakistan and China, the aircraft must also be able to operate in high-altitude locations and from temporary or unpaved strips. Besides ferrying troops, vehicles and ammunition, India also uses military transport aircraft for disaster relief and humanitarian assistance.

The bids are due by early December, after which the proposals will go through technical evaluation.

Amid its two decade-long push for greater local production and technology transfer, the government wants the mega aviation contract to deepen the country’s defense manufacturing footprint.
items.summaryZh: 新德里——为强化本国的航空航天工业基础，印度政府希望将这笔价值约105亿美元的印度空军60架中型运输机采购合同授予巴西航空工业公司或美国洛克希德·马丁公司中的某一方，同时要求这些企业在印度扩建飞机制造设施。
items.titleZh: 巴西航空工业公司与洛克希德·马丁公司竞逐印度105亿美元军用运输机采购合同
zhParas: 新德里——来自巴西的巴西航空工业公司与美国洛克希德·马丁公司均在争取那份价值约105亿美元的印度空军60架中型运输机采购合同，同时提出要在印度扩建飞机制造设施。
本段译文为：印度正在寻求更换那些已经老旧的军用运输机队，其中包括苏联时代制造的安-32飞机，而巴西航空工业公司的C-390“千禧”型号正与洛克希德·马丁公司的C-130J“超级大力神”型号展开竞争，争夺这份价值约105亿美元的采购合同。
今年8月，印度向五家本土企业发出了招标请求，正式开启了争夺该国规模最大的军用航空采购合同之一的竞争。由于新德里方面规定，首批多用途军用运输机需直接交付即可投入使用，而其余机型则必须由印度国内企业自行制造，因此全球航空企业纷纷选择与印度公司展开合作。
鉴于印度致力于建立本土航空航天工业体系，巴西航空工业公司已于10月1日宣布，若能中标该合同，该公司将与印度合作伙伴马欣德拉国防公司共同选择印度中部城市那格浦尔作为该军用运输机的生产基地。
巴西航空工业公司国防与安全业务板块的总裁兼首席执行官博斯科·达科斯塔·朱尼尔在与马欣德拉公司的联合声明中表示：“将那格浦尔定为军用运输机组装厂的候选地点，是印度构建强大、可持续的航空航天产业生态体系的重要一步。
这两家公司表示，他们将逐步将印度航空航天企业纳入C-390 Millennium产品体系，为其提供制造、培训以及全生命周期支持服务。
洛克希德·马丁公司已在印度设有业务布局——印度空军目前运营着12架C-130J“超级大力神”运输机。该公司表示，其此次推出的C-130J-30型号属于8.1.2版本，其性能将优于印度空军现有的那些飞机。
若中标，洛克希德·马丁公司表示将在美国生产12架该型军用运输机，同时与旗下合资企业塔塔先进系统有限公司合作在印度生产48架。
这家美国公司已在印度建立了制造基地，其与塔塔公司合作在当地生产该军用运输机的关键部件，包括尾翼组件等。
洛克希德·马丁公司全球业务发展与战略高级副总裁丹·特尼最近向《印度新闻信托报》表示，若能赢得这笔价值105亿美元的军用运输机订单，该公司便能在印度建立更庞大的产业布局。
他与塔塔公司有着长期的合作伙伴关系，后者负责为C-130J飞机生产各类零部件及尾翼结构。他称，这一强大的生产能力将在我们此次的投标中得到进一步发挥。
该企业还提议对印度空军现有的12架C-130J运输机进行升级。
印度为该军用运输机设定了至少40%的国产部件比例要求。由于该国与竞争对手巴基斯坦和中国有着漫长的喜马拉雅山脉边界，这类飞机还必须能够在高海拔地区以及临时或未铺设跑道的简易机场起降。除了用于运送部队、车辆和弹药外，印度还会利用军用运输机执行救灾与人道主义援助任务。
投标截止日期为12月初，此后相关提案将接受技术评估。
在长达二十年的推动本土化生产与技术转移的努力背景下，印度政府希望借此巨额军用航空采购合同进一步壮大本国的国防制造业实力。

items.title: A life defined by service and grace
items.author: MAJ Travis Mueller
items.summary: Nicom’s 25-year career reflects a legacy of service defined by storytelling, servant leadership, grace and commitment to her community.
items.body:
BAUMHOLDER, Germany — 1st Sgt. HollyAnn Nicom’s roots of military service reach back generations.

Her grandfather served in the Army during World War I. Her father was drafted into the Army during the Korean War. Near the end of her father’s life, as early-onset Alzheimer’s disease took away many of his memories, there were still things he remembered, like his dog tag number and the words to “Over There,” a song associated with WWI.

When he died in February 2001, Nicom wanted to better understand the pride he held in being a veteran.

“I wanted to do something to know him better and understand his pride as a veteran,” Nicom said. “I know how important his Army service was to him.”

A chance encounter with a recruiter at an ice cream shop introduced Nicom to the Pennsylvania Army National Guard. She began the enlistment process shortly before Sept. 11, 2001. After the attacks, and knowing fully what she was signing up for, she returned to the Military Entrance Processing Station a month later after receiving a needed medical waiver.

“The gravity of what I was doing, and the sense of pride that went along with it felt much different when I went back that second time,” Nicom said.

Now, nearly 25 years later, Nicom serves as the senior enlisted leader for the 109th Mobile Public Affairs Detachment, currently deployed to Germany in support of U.S. Special Operations Command Europe. Her career has included work as a motor transport operator, deployments to Kuwait and Iraq, domestic-response missions following Hurricane Katrina, support to U.S. Customs and Border Protection during Operation Jump Start and public-affairs assignments in Latvia, Germany and Tunisia.

Throughout those experiences, Nicom said she has retained the same commitment she felt when she first raised her right hand.

“Throughout my 25-year military career, I have not lost that sense of pride and commitment to my obligation,” Nicom said.

Nicom’s connection to public affairs began before she formally entered the career field. While deployed as a truck driver, she routinely carried a camera and photographed the missions and Soldiers around her. Her goal was simply to capture those significant moments of her own life. What she found was that she was capturing a larger piece of history.

“I was able to capture photographs depicting what it was like to be on mission in a war zone,” Nicom said. “Inadvertently, I told the story of the Soldiers around me through imagery before I even knew what public affairs was.”

Those experiences later shaped her understanding of public affairs as both a way to preserve history and keep the public informed. Her work has earned recognition in the Maj. Gen. Keith L. Ware Communications Awards Competition at the National Guard Bureau and the Pennsylvania National Guard levels, but Nicom places equal value on helping other Soldiers develop.

As a first sergeant, she said effective leadership means creating an environment where Soldiers have room to be creative, can think beyond the expected solution and have the resources they need to succeed.

“In a unit made up of storytellers and communicators, a good enlisted leader allows room for the creativity to flow,” Nicom said.

Staff Sgt. Dave Thomson, a public affairs specialist in the 109th MPAD, said Nicom’s leadership is most evident in the routine work that keeps the unit moving. Whether the task is transportation or cleaning latrines, he said Nicom works alongside Soldiers rather than simply directing them.

Thomson recalled Soldiers from a different unit expressing surprise when they saw the 109th MPAD’s first sergeant taking out trash one day. Usually a task like that is delegated to a junior Soldier.

“If there was a person who was an example of a servant leader, she would definitely be it,” Thomson said. “I think she’s inspirational in and out of the Army.”

As the unit’s first sergeant, Nicom helps set and enforce standards while remaining attentive to the individual circumstances affecting Soldiers. She believes accountability is necessary, but discipline should also leave room for a Soldier to learn, recover and continue contributing to the team.

Her leadership approach is grounded in a belief that Soldiers should not be defined solely by their mistakes. Nicom said leaders must hold Soldiers accountable while also recognizing their potential and treating them with empathy.

“Sometimes, the answer is to show them, with grace, their importance within the unit and that they can do better,” Nicom said. “I have seen noncommissioned officers who have made very poor choices turn their entire mindset around once they are counseled with empathy and grace.”

Sgt. 1st Class Brandon Nelson, the 109th MPAD’s readiness and administrative NCO, said Nicom consistently puts that principle into practice.

Nelson said Nicom has shown more grace to some Soldiers than he may have initially expected, but he respects her ability to seek out the good in people.

“In the true essence of grace and giving unearned ‘love, blessings, forgiveness,’ she’s definitely shown patience and understanding with multiple members of the group,” Nelson said. “I think the theme of ‘People’ is where she routinely has and keeps a positive outlook and searches for good.”

Her faith informs that mindset. Nicom said the message of Matthew 25:40, demonstrating faith through acts of kindness, guides how she leads, serves and interacts with Soldiers.

She makes a point to remember birthdays, recognize personal interests, encourage public-affairs strengths and praise missions done well. Whether during routine unit operations or on deployment in Europe, Nicom said she tries to lead with the same kindness and grace she would want from her own leaders.

That commitment to service extends far beyond the formation.

After returning from her combat deployments, Nicom remembered Vietnam veterans waiting at the airport to welcome her units home. Their support left a lasting impression, particularly because many Vietnam veterans did not receive the same reception after their own service.

“I so badly wanted to thank them for their service and reciprocate the ‘welcome home,’” Nicom said.

More than a decade ago, she made the decision to become an anonymous living liver donor, specifying that her donation be given to a Vietnam veteran. The process took about a year, including extensive testing and multiple trips to Yale New Haven Hospital in Connecticut.

Nicom selected her enlistment anniversary as the date of the surgery. She donated approximately 60% of her liver to a Marine Corps Vietnam veteran she had never met.

“I wanted it to be a ‘thank you and welcome home’ gift from a grateful nation,” Nicom said.

The recipient was near death before the transplant. Although the two have never met, they exchange letters several times a year. Nicom said he was able to walk his granddaughter down the aisle at her wedding last year.

Nicom also volunteers in her community, including work supporting English-language learners, hospice residents and local community activities. She describes herself as someone who roots for the underdog and believes in paying forward the support she has received from others.

“Every single person in the world has been in a position, at one time or another, where they have needed support, encouragement or a helping hand,” Nicom said. “I have been on the receiving end of a helping hand a few times in my life, and I’m a big proponent of paying it forward.”

Whether serving in uniform, at work or in her community, Nicom hopes her example reinforces the importance of genuine care for others.

“At the end of the day, people in your life, including Soldiers, remember the times you came through for them and they remember the times you let them down,” Nicom said. “I hope I am remembered as someone who was positive, dependable and uplifted those around me through genuine encouragement.”
items.summaryZh: 霍莉安·尼科姆拥有25年的军旅生涯，她的从军传统源自数代之前的家族传统，其职业生涯始终以善于讲述故事、奉行服务型领导风格、举止优雅，以及对所在社区的奉献精神为特色。
items.titleZh: 以奉献与优雅诠释的一生
zhParas: 德国鲍姆霍尔德——一等军士霍莉安·尼科姆的从军传统可追溯至数代之前。
她的祖父在第一次世界大战期间服役于陆军，父亲则在朝鲜战争期间应征入伍。在父亲生命即将走到尽头时，尽管早发性阿尔茨海默病夺走了他许多记忆，但他仍记得一些事情，比如自己的军牌编号，以及与第一次世界大战相关的歌曲《Over There》的歌词。
2001年2月其父亲去世时，尼科姆希望能更深入地理解父亲作为退伍军人所怀有的那份自豪感。
尼科姆说：‘我希望能做点什么来更深入地了解他，理解他作为退伍军人所怀有的那份自豪感。我知道他在军队服役对他而言有多重要。’
一次在冰淇淋店偶遇征兵人员的经历让尼科姆认识了宾夕法尼亚州陆军国民自卫队。她在2001年9月11日袭击事件发生前不久开始了入伍流程。在了解袭击的严重性以及入伍意味着要承担的任务后，她在获得必要的医疗豁免许可一个月后，再次回到军事入伍处理站完成相关手续。
第二次回到那里时，我意识到自己所从事工作的重大意义，以及随之而来的自豪感，都与第一次截然不同，”尼科姆说道。
如今，近25年过去了，尼科姆现任第109机动公共事务分队的高级士官领导，该分队目前驻扎在德国，为美军欧洲特种作战司令部提供支援。她的职业生涯涵盖过汽车运输操作员的工作，还曾赴科威特和伊拉克执行任务，在“卡特里娜”飓风过后参与国内救援行动，在“启动行动”期间为美国海关及边境保护局提供协助，此外还在拉脱维亚、德国和突尼斯承担过公共事务相关工作。
尼科姆表示，在经历所有这些任务之后，她依然保持着当初举起右手宣誓时那份坚定的决心。
尼科姆表示：‘在长达25年的军旅生涯中，我始终没有丧失那份自豪感，也从未放弃对自己职责的坚守。’
在正式步入军旅生涯之前，尼科姆就已经开始关注公共事务。在担任卡车司机期间，她总是随身携带相机，记录下各项军事行动以及身边的士兵们。她的初衷仅仅是留住自己生命中那些重要的时刻，却未曾预料到自己正在记录下更宏大的历史篇章。
这些经历让她逐渐认识到，公共事务工作既是传承历史、向公众传递信息的重要途径。她的出色表现曾获得国民自卫队总局及宾夕法尼亚州国民自卫队举办的基思·L·韦尔传播奖竞赛的认可，但尼科姆同样重视帮助其他军人成长。
作为一名一级军士长，她认为有效的领导力在于营造一种环境，让士兵们有空间发挥创造力，能够跳出常规思维寻找解决方案，并获得取得成功所需的资源。
尼科姆表示：“在这样一个由擅长讲故事和沟通的人组成的部队里，一位优秀的士兵领袖会为成员的创造力发挥留出空间。
第109宪兵航空旅的公共事务专家戴夫·汤姆森军士长表示，尼科姆的领导风格在维持部队正常运转的日常工作中体现得最为明显。无论是在物资运输还是清理厕所这类任务中，她总是与士兵们并肩工作，而非仅仅发号施令。
汤姆森回忆说，有一次其他部队的士兵看到第109宪兵航空旅的首席军士正在清理垃圾时，都感到十分惊讶。通常这类任务都是交给下级士兵来完成的。
汤森森表示：‘如果要说谁是服务型领导者的典范，那非她莫属。’他进一步称：‘无论在军队内外，她都堪称激励人心的人物。’
作为该部队的首席军士，尼科姆在制定并执行各项标准的同时，也会关注每位士兵的个体状况。她认为责任意识固然重要，但纪律措施也应给予士兵学习、恢复状态并继续为团队做贡献的空间。
尼科姆的领导理念建立在这样一种信念之上：士兵不应仅因其过错而被定义。她认为，领导者必须在要求士兵承担责任的同时，看到他们的潜力，并以同理心对待他们。
尼科姆表示：“有时候，正确的做法是以温和的方式让他们明白自己在部队中的重要性，以及他们完全有能力做得更好。我曾见过一些做出了极其错误决定的士官，在得到充满同理心且温和的劝导后，彻底改变了他们的思维方式。
第109宪兵装甲旅的战备与行政事务军士长布兰登·纳尔逊表示，尼科姆始终将这一原则付诸实践。
纳尔逊表示，尼科姆对某些士兵展现出的宽容与体谅超出了他最初的预期，但他很钦佩她善于发现他人优点的能力。
纳尔逊表示：‘从她那种充满恩惠与无私给予‘爱、祝福与宽恕’的特质来看，她无疑对团队中的多名成员展现出了极大的耐心与理解。’他进一步指出：‘我认为‘以人为本’正是她始终保持积极心态、善于发现他人优点的核心所在。’
尼科姆总是牢记每个人的生日，关注他们的个人兴趣，鼓励他们发挥在公共事务方面的优势，并对完成得出色的任务给予表扬。无论是在部队的常规行动中，还是在欧洲执行任务时，她都努力以自己期望从上级那里得到的那种友善与优雅来领导团队。
这种服务精神并非仅限于部队内部，更延伸至更广阔的范畴。
从执行作战任务归来后，尼科姆回忆起那些在机场等候、欢迎她所率领的部队归来的越南战争老兵们。他们的支持给她留下了深刻的印象，尤其是因为许多越南战争老兵在完成服役后并未得到过同样的欢迎。
我真心想感谢他们的奉献，也想要以同样的方式回报他们迎接我归来的那份热情，”尼科姆说道。
十多年前，她决定成为一名匿名活体肝脏捐献者，并明确要求将自己的肝脏捐献给一名越南战争老兵。整个捐献流程耗时约一年，期间她需要接受多项检查，还多次前往康涅狄格州的耶鲁纽黑文医院。
尼科姆选择在她的入伍纪念日接受手术，她将自己肝脏中约60%的份额捐献给了那位她从未谋面的越南战争时期的海军陆战队老兵。
我希望这是一份来自一个心怀感激的国家的‘感谢您，欢迎回家’的礼物，”尼科姆说道。
在接受移植手术之前，这名受助者已处于生命垂危状态。尽管两人从未见过面，但他们仍每年互通数封信件。尼科姆表示，去年在孙女婚礼上，他得以亲自陪着孙女走过婚礼的红毯。
尼科姆还积极参与社区志愿服务，为英语学习者提供帮助、照顾临终病人，以及参与各类本地社区活动。她自称是那些愿意支持弱势群体的人，也坚信应当将他人给予自己的帮助传递下去。
无论是在军装之下执行任务、在职场工作，还是参与社区服务，尼科姆都希望自己能以身作则，让人们更加认识到真诚关怀他人至关重要。

items.title: Grave of Cornish soldier missing since 1945 identified in Germany
items.summary: A rededication service for Private (Pte) Sidney Allen was organised by the MOD’s ‘War Detectives’ at CWGC Reichswald Forest War Cemetery, Germany.
items.body:
The previously unnamed grave of a World War 2 soldier from Saltash, Cornwall, who served with the Hampshire Regiment been identified and rededicated in his name 81 years after his death.

The service for Pte Sidney Allen was organised by the MOD ’s ‘War Detectives’ at CWGC Reichswald Forest War Cemetery, Germany.

JCCC Caseworker, Nicola Nash, said:

It is a great privilege to be here to honour Pte Sidney Allen, who gave his life in service to his country at just 19 years of age. For more than 80 years his family did not know exactly where he lay, making this identification especially significant. Today we remember his sacrifice and ensure that his name, service and story are never forgotten.

Private Allen grew up in Saltash working in HM Dockyard alongside his father. He enlisted in the Army in February 1944 and arrived in France that August, joining the 7th Battalion, Hampshire Regiment, during the Allied advance through Normandy.

Over the following months he took part in several operations including the capture of Mont Picon and St-Denis-de-Mere, the advance across the River Seine, the liberation of Brussels, Operation Market Garden, and fighting in the Netherlands and Germany.

In February 1945, the battalion joined Operation Veritable, the offensive to clear the Reichswald Forest, where soldiers faced fierce resistance, deep mud and flooded terrain. On 15 February 1945, during heavy fighting near Cleve and the Reichswald, Sidney was killed aged 19 and officially recorded as missing.

Decades later, research submitted by a member of the public established that he had originally been buried in Materborn alongside other soldiers killed in the same action. As the only member of the battalion from that engagement still listed as missing, the grave was finally identified as belonging to Private Sidney Allen.

The headstone was replaced by Commonwealth War Graves Commission ( CWGC ).

Fergus Read, Commemorations Case Officer at the CWGC , said:

It is deeply fitting that Private Sidney Allen is now commemorated by name at his final resting place. The evidence for the grave identification was compelling, and Private Allen, who was previously commemorated on a memorial, now has a known grave, which the Commission will care for in perpetuity.
items.summaryZh: 在德国的莱希斯瓦尔德森林战争公墓，英国国防部旗下的“战争侦探”团队为西德尼·艾伦二等兵举办了重新献祭仪式，以纪念这位来自康沃尔郡萨尔塔什、曾服役于汉普郡团的二战士兵。
items.titleZh: 1945年以来失踪的康沃尔郡士兵墓地在德国被确认身份
zhParas: 在这名来自康沃尔郡萨尔塔什、曾服役于汉普郡团的二战士兵去世81年后，其此前未被标注姓名的坟墓终于被确认身份，英国国防部旗下的“战争侦探”团队在德国的莱希斯瓦尔德森林战争公墓为他举行了重新献祭仪式。
在德国的莱希斯瓦尔德森林战争公墓，英国国防部旗下的“战争侦探”团队为西德尼·艾伦二等兵举办了重新献祭仪式。
JCCC的个案处理员尼古拉·纳什表示：
能够在此缅怀19岁便为祖国献出生命的西德尼·艾伦下士，我们深感荣幸。在80多年的时间里，他的家人一直不知道他的安葬地点，因此此次找到他的墓地具有格外重要的意义。今天，我们缅怀他的牺牲，确保他的名字、他的奉献以及他的故事永远不会被遗忘。
艾伦下士在萨尔塔什长大，与父亲一起在皇家造船厂工作。1944年2月他应征入伍，同年8月抵达法国，在盟军穿越诺曼底时加入了汉普郡团的第七营。
在之后的几个月里，他参与了多场作战行动，包括夺取蒙皮康和圣德尼德梅尔、渡过塞纳河推进、解放布鲁塞尔、市场花园行动，以及在荷兰和德国的战斗。
1945年2月，该营参与了旨在清除赖希斯瓦尔德森林的“真诚行动”，在作战中士兵们遭遇了顽强的抵抗，同时还面临泥泞不堪及被水淹没的恶劣地形。1945年2月15日，在克莱夫附近及赖希斯瓦尔德森林一带的激烈战斗中，19岁的西德尼阵亡，官方记录将其列为失踪人员。
数十年后，一位民众提交的研究成果证实，西德尼·艾伦最初是与在同次作战中阵亡的其他士兵一同被安葬在马特博恩。由于他是那次战斗中该营中唯一仍被列为失踪人员的士兵，其墓地最终被确认为西德尼·艾伦下士的安葬地。
该墓碑已由英联邦战争墓地委员会更换。

如今，西德尼·艾伦列兵的最终安息之地终于有了刻有他名字的纪念标识，这实在是一件无比恰当的事。用于确认其墓地身份的证据十分确凿，此前仅以纪念牌形式被纪念的艾伦列兵如今终于有了确切的墓址，而英联邦战争墓地委员会也将永久负责维护这座墓地。

items.title: 'Unknown' Sheffield soldier named in Netherlands Ceremony
items.summary: The previously un-named grave of a World War 2 soldier has been identified and rededicated in his name in a service 81 years after his death.
items.body:
A soldier in an unmarked grave has been identified as Sheffield-born LCpl Ronald Smirthwaite who was killed in the Netherlands in 1945.

For years LCpl Smirthwaite was commemorated on the Groesbeek Memorial as one of those World War 2 dead missing with no known grave.

Now, following extensive research, MOD investigators have now confirmed that the grave in Jonkerbos War Cemetery can now be marked with his name.

A rededication service for LCpl Smirthwaite was organised by the MOD ’s Joint Casualty and Compassionate Centre’s ( JCCC ) ‘War Detectives’.

JCCC Caseworker, Tracey Bowers, said:

“Ronald Smirthwaite was a proud Yorkshireman whose life was cut short during the final months of the World War 2. This rededication service restores his identity, recognises his Yorkshire roots and ensures that future generations understand his ultimate sacrifice.”

Ronald joined the Army on 4 May 1944, initially into the General Service Corps employed as a blacksmith’s striker, an occupation described as providing the muscle to the blacksmith’s skilled work.

Padre Paul Garnell who conducted the service said:

LCpl Ronald Smirthwaite after many years of being an “unknown soldier” is now known and will forever be memorialised and remembered along with his colleagues. This has only been possible due to the hard work and dedication by many.

The investigation was examined by the MOD and The National Army Museum following submissions by an Officer of the Royal Netherlands Army and a member of the public.

Records from the Hallamshire Battalion describe a fierce engagement on 22 February 1945 after which LCpl Smirthwaite was reported missing and presumed killed in action. It later emerged that he had been captured alive but seriously wounded and was lost while attempting to escape. His body had been recovered and buried before being reburied as an unknown soldier.

His headstone was replaced by one engraved with his name by the Commonwealth War Graves Commission ( CWGC ).

Polly Brewster, Commemorations Case Officer at the CWGC , said:

We are honoured to have worked with the Royal Netherlands Army, the Ministry of Defence and the National Army Museum to identify Ronald Smirthwaite’s final resting place. Eighty-one years after he fell, and after decades of uncertainty for his family and loved ones, it feels deeply poignant to be able to commemorate him at the site of his grave with a new, named headstone. His sacrifice will not be forgotten.
items.summaryZh: 在那名二战士兵逝世81年后，人们终于确认了那座此前没有标识的坟墓的主人的身份——他便是出生于谢菲尔德的罗纳德·斯米尔思韦特下士，他于1945年在荷兰阵亡，如今人们已为这座坟墓正式命名并举行了纪念仪式。
items.titleZh: 荷兰举行的纪念仪式上，那名身份不明的谢菲尔德士兵终于获知其身份
zhParas: 那座无标识坟墓中的士兵已被确认为出生于谢菲尔德的罗纳德·斯米尔思韦特下士，他于1945年在荷兰阵亡。
多年来，斯米尔思韦特下士一直作为那些在第二次世界大战中阵亡但无确切墓地的失踪士兵之一，被安葬在赫罗斯贝克纪念碑上接受纪念。
经过深入调查，英国国防部调查人员现已确认，琼克博斯战争公墓中的那座墓碑可以刻上这名士兵的名字。
英国国防部下属的联合伤员与抚恤中心“战争侦探”小组为斯米尔思韦特下士举办了重新命名仪式。
JCCC的个案处理员特蕾西·鲍尔斯表示：
罗纳德·斯米思韦特是一位来自约克郡的骄傲的英国人，他在第二次世界大战的最后几个月里英年早逝。此次重新为他的坟墓举行仪式，不仅明确了他的身份，也彰显了他来自约克郡的根源，同时能让后代了解他为战争做出的巨大牺牲。
罗纳德于1944年5月4日加入陆军，最初被分配到总务兵团，担任铁匠帮工，这一工作被视为为铁匠的精湛技艺提供体力支撑。
主持此次仪式的保罗·加内尔神父表示：
多年来一直被列为“无名士兵”的罗纳德·斯米尔思韦特下士如今终于有了身份，他将与战友们一同被永久铭记在历史中。这一成果的取得，离不开众多人的辛勤努力与奉献。
在荷兰皇家陆军一名军官及一名普通民众的举报之后，英国国防部与国家陆军博物馆对这起事件展开了调查。
根据哈勒姆郡营的记录，1945年2月22日曾发生过一场激烈的战斗，战后有消息称斯米尔思韦特下士失踪，据推测已阵亡。后来人们发现他其实被俘虏了，虽然伤势严重，但在试图逃脱时走失。他的遗体虽曾被找回并安葬，却又作为无名士兵被重新安葬。
英联邦战争墓地委员会已用刻有其姓名的新墓碑替换了那块旧墓碑。
CWGC的纪念事务负责人波莉·布鲁斯特表示：
我们很荣幸能与荷兰皇家陆军、荷兰国防部以及国家陆军博物馆通力合作，最终找到了罗纳德·斯密思韦特的安葬地。在他牺牲81年后，也在他的家人和亲友历经数十年迷茫之后，如今能够在他的墓前立起刻有其姓名的新墓碑来纪念他，实在令人感慨万千。他的牺牲必将永被铭记。

items.title: Why Financial Stability Matters for Military Readiness
items.author: admin
items.summary: Military readiness requires preparation for the unexpected. Airmen and Guardians train for changing conditions, demanding assignments and missions that can shift with little notice. But readiness extends beyond what happens on duty. Having a strong financial foundation at home can... The post Why Financial Stability Matters for Military Readiness appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .
items.body:
Military readiness requires preparation for the unexpected. Airmen and Guardians train for changing conditions, demanding assignments and missions that can shift with little notice. But readiness extends beyond what happens on duty. Having a strong financial foundation at home can help servicemembers create enough flexibility to handle the unexpected when it happens.

“While you can’t predict every expense or know exactly when the next set of orders, PCS move, deployment or unexpected challenge will come, you can prepare for it,” said Thomas Racca, manager of personal finance management at Navy Federal Credit Union. “It starts with the financial habits you build every day. Having savings set aside, understanding where your money is going and keeping debt manageable can reduce stress and give you the flexibility to adapt when plans change.”

An emergency fund is one of the most important places to start. Setting aside even a small portion of each paycheck can gradually create a cushion for costs that weren’t part of the plan, whether that’s an unexpected car repair, a temporary housing gap or expenses associated with a move. The goal doesn’t have to be saving a large amount all at once. Consistently setting aside what you can helps build that cushion over time.

Once you’ve built a base level of savings, making a plan, such as creating a realistic budget, to tackle high-interest debt can free up more room in your budget. Understanding military benefits provided by financial institutions is another important part of that foundation. Additionally, programs such as housing allowances, relocation support and the Post-9/11 GI Bill can help offset some major life expenses. Knowing what benefits are available and how they fit into your budget can help you make the most of your income while continuing to save for longer-term goals.

Not every dollar in savings serves the same purpose, either. Money that may be needed for a PCS, emergency or another near-term expense is generally best kept in an account that’s accessible, such as a savings account. Money that won’t be needed right away may be better suited for a certificate, which can be a great way to grow your savings over a set term.

The right approach can also vary over time. A new assignment, promotion, deployment or growing family can all change what a household needs from its budget. Rather than setting a financial plan once and forgetting about it, make a habit of checking in on your spending, savings and debt and adjusting as circumstances change.

“Just like readiness is built through preparation, financial confidence is built through habits,” said Racca. “Tracking your spending, growing your emergency savings and managing debt may seem like small steps, but they create a stronger foundation for whatever comes next. The most important thing is to start. Take 15 minutes this week to review your spending, identify one area where you can save a little more and make a plan for that money before it gets spent.”

Navy Federal offers financial resources designed to help members put those habits into practice throughout different stages of military life. Members can use My MakingCents™ to see their Navy Federal accounts alongside accounts at other financial institutions, create a budget, track spending, monitor credit and manage recurring payments in one place.

“We often talk about readiness in terms of training and preparation, but financial readiness is part of that equation too. When your finances are in order, you can spend less time worrying about money and more time focusing on your mission, your family and your future,” added Racca.

Financial readiness isn’t about having every expense mapped out or knowing exactly what the next set of orders will bring. It’s about having the financial foundation to adapt when plans change. For Airmen, Guardians, and their Families, building that foundation today can mean being better prepared for whatever comes next.

This content is intended to provide general information and should not be considered legal, tax, or financial advice. It is always a good idea to consult a tax or financial advisor for specific information on how certain laws apply to your situation and about your individual financial situation.
items.summaryZh: 军队的战备状态意味着要为各种意外情况做好准备。空军官兵与海军战士们不断训练，以应对可能随时发生变化的作战环境以及突如其来的任务要求。不过，战备的意义并不仅限于执行任务期间。如果家庭经济状况稳固，军人就能拥有足够的灵活性，以便在意外状况出现时从容应对。
items.titleZh: 为何经济稳定对军队的战备状态至关重要
zhParas: 军队的战备状态意味着要为各种意外情况做好准备。空军官兵与海军战士们不断训练，以应对可能随时发生变化的作战环境以及突如其来的任务要求。不过，战备的意义并不仅限于执行任务期间。如果家庭经济状况稳固，军人就能拥有足够的灵活性，以便在意外状况出现时从容应对。
海军联邦信用社的个人财务管理经理托马斯·拉卡表示：‘虽然我们无法预知所有的开支，也无法确切知道下一批指令、调动命令、部署任务或突发挑战何时会出现，但我们完全可以为此做好准备。’他进一步指出，这一切都始于日常养成的财务习惯——预留足够的储蓄、清楚了解资金去向并控制债务规模，不仅能减轻压力，还能在计划发生变化时让军人拥有足够的灵活性来应对。’
应急基金是建立财务安全垫的最重要途径之一。即便从每笔工资中抽出少量资金，也能逐步为那些计划之外的高额支出做好准备，比如意外的汽车维修费、暂时的住房短缺问题，或是搬迁相关的各项开销。无需一次性存下巨额资金，只要坚持定期储蓄，久而久之就能积累起足够的财务缓冲能力。
在建立起基础储蓄之后，通过制定合理的预算等计划来偿还高息债务，就能为预算腾出更多空间。了解金融机构提供的军人专属福利也是构建财务安全基础的重要环节。此外，住房补贴、搬迁援助以及“9·11”后的军人福利法案等各类政策，也能帮助抵消生活中的重大开支。清楚有哪些福利可用，以及它们如何与个人预算相匹配，便能帮助人们在维持日常开支的同时，继续为长远目标储蓄。
并非所有的储蓄资金都能用于相同的目的。那些可能用于调动工作、应对紧急情况或其他短期开支的资金，最好存放在便于取用的账户中，比如普通储蓄账户。而那些短期内不会用到的钱，则更适合存入定期存单，这是在固定期限内让储蓄实现增值的不错方式。
合适的财务规划方式也会随时间而变化。新的工作任务、晋升机会、部署任务或是家庭规模的扩大，都可能改变家庭在预算上的需求。与其一次性制定好财务计划后就不再调整，不如养成定期审视支出、储蓄状况及债务情况的习惯，并根据实际情况及时作出调整。
拉卡表示：“正如战备状态是通过各项准备工作的积累而形成的，财务稳定感也是通过日常习惯养成的。追踪开支、增加应急储蓄以及管理债务看似都是些微不足道的举措，但它们能为未来可能出现的各种情况奠定更坚实的基础。最重要的是要迈出第一步——本周就花15分钟时间梳理一下自己的开支情况，找出一个可以进一步节省开支的领域，然后为这笔钱制定一个合理的使用计划，避免其被随意挥霍。
海军联邦银行提供了各类金融服务，旨在帮助军人在军旅生涯的不同阶段将良好的财务习惯付诸实践。军人可通过“My MakingCents™”平台将海军联邦银行的账户与其他金融机构的账户集中管理，同时制定预算、追踪支出、监控信用状况，并统一处理各类定期付款事务。
拉卡补充称：‘我们通常将战备状态与训练和准备工作联系在一起，但财务方面的准备同样是其中不可或缺的一部分。一旦财务状况稳定，人们就能减少为金钱发愁的时间，从而将更多精力投入到任务执行、家庭照顾以及未来规划上。’
财务方面的战备准备并非指要将每一笔开支都精确规划，或是提前知晓下一项指令会带来什么，而是指拥有能够在计划发生变化时迅速做出调整的财务基础。对于空军军人、国民警卫队成员及其家属而言，如今就奠定这样的财务基础，意味着能为未来可能出现的各种情况做好更充分的准备。
本文仅旨在提供一般性信息，不应被视为法律、税务或财务建议。针对特定法律条款如何适用于您的具体情况以及您的个人财务状况，咨询税务或财务顾问始终是更为稳妥的做法。

军队的战备状态意味着要为各种意外情况做好准备。空军官兵与海军战士们不断训练，以应对可能随时发生变化的作战环境以及突如其来的任务要求。不过，战备的意义并不仅限于执行任务期间。如果家庭经济状况稳固，军人就能拥有足够的灵活性，以便在意外状况出现时从容应对。

海军联邦信用社的个人财务管理经理托马斯·拉卡表示：‘虽然我们无法预知所有的开支，也无法确切知道下一批指令、调动命令、部署任务或突发挑战何时会出现，但我们完全可以为此做好准备。’他进一步指出，这一切都始于日常养成的财务习惯——预留足够的储蓄、清楚了解资金去向并控制债务规模，不仅能减轻压力，还能在计划发生变化时让军人拥有足够的灵活性来应对。’

应急基金是建立财务安全垫的最重要途径之一。即便从每笔工资中抽出少量资金，也能逐步为那些计划之外的高额支出做好准备，比如意外的汽车维修费、暂时的住房短缺问题，或是搬迁相关的各项开销。无需一次性存下巨额资金，只要坚持定期储蓄，久而久之就能积累起足够的财务缓冲能力。

在建立起基础储蓄之后，通过制定合理的预算等计划来偿还高息债务，就能为预算腾出更多空间。了解金融机构提供的军人专属福利也是构建财务安全基础的重要环节。此外，住房补贴、搬迁援助以及“9·11”后的军人福利法案等各类政策，也能帮助抵消生活中的重大开支。清楚有哪些福利可用，以及它们如何与个人预算相匹配，便能帮助人们在维持日常开支的同时，继续为长远目标储蓄。

并非所有的储蓄资金都能用于相同的目的。那些可能用于调动工作、应对紧急情况或其他短期开支的资金，最好存放在便于取用的账户中，比如普通储蓄账户。而那些短期内不会用到的钱，则更适合存入定期存单，这是在固定期限内让储蓄实现增值的不错方式。

合适的财务规划方式也会随时间而变化。新的工作任务、晋升机会、部署任务或是家庭规模的扩大，都可能改变家庭在预算上的需求。与其一次性制定好财务计划后就不再调整，不如养成定期审视支出、储蓄状况及债务情况的习惯，并根据实际情况及时作出调整。

拉卡表示：“正如战备状态是通过各项准备工作的积累而形成的，财务稳定感也是通过日常习惯养成的。追踪开支、增加应急储蓄以及管理债务看似都是些微不足道的举措，但它们能为未来可能出现的各种情况奠定更坚实的基础。最重要的是要迈出第一步——本周就花15分钟时间梳理一下自己的开支情况，找出一个可以进一步节省开支的领域，然后为这笔钱制定一个合理的使用计划，避免其被随意挥霍。

海军联邦银行提供了各类金融服务，旨在帮助军人在军旅生涯的不同阶段将良好的财务习惯付诸实践。军人可通过“My MakingCents™”平台将海军联邦银行的账户与其他金融机构的账户集中管理，同时制定预算、追踪支出、监控信用状况，并统一处理各类定期付款事务。

拉卡补充称：‘我们通常将战备状态与训练和准备工作联系在一起，但财务方面的准备同样是其中不可或缺的一部分。一旦财务状况稳定，人们就能减少为金钱发愁的时间，从而将更多精力投入到任务执行、家庭照顾以及未来规划上。’

财务方面的战备准备并非指要将每一笔开支都精确规划，或是提前知晓下一项指令会带来什么，而是指拥有能够在计划发生变化时迅速做出调整的财务基础。对于空军军人、国民警卫队成员及其家属而言，如今就奠定这样的财务基础，意味着能为未来可能出现的各种情况做好更充分的准备。

本文仅旨在提供一般性信息，不应被视为法律、税务或财务建议。针对特定法律条款如何适用于您的具体情况以及您的个人财务状况，咨询税务或财务顾问始终是更为稳妥的做法。

items.title: Research Priorities for Robust Climate Assessments in the United States
items.author: Benjamin Lee Preston
items.summary: This research priorities roadmap aims to catalyze collaborations, research, and a network of climate assessments to synthesize the state of climate impacts and to provide accessible information for climate action plans and decisions in the U.S.
items.body:
Expert InsightsPosted on rand.org Oct 7, 2026Published in: Earth's Future, Volume 14, Issue 9, e2025EF007336 (September 2026). DOI: 10.1029/2025EF007336

Scientific assessments play a critical role in synthesizing evidence to support evidence-based decision-making in many sectors and topics. For climate change, large-scale assessments like the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) and the United States (U.S.) National Climate Assessment (NCA) reports help many different users—from national government to local governments, Indigenous Peoples and communities, the private sector, the social sector, and the scientific community itself—navigate the complex field of climate risks, impacts, and integrated solutions. While co-creation with users is essential to developing actionable assessments, this paper lays the groundwork for future processes by identifying many advancing and emerging areas of relevant knowledge ready for assessment or additional near-term research. Drawing on the expertise of many scholars who were formerly tasked with producing the Sixth NCA and authors of other national or sub-national climate assessment reports, this paper highlights select U.S.-relevant topics in which research advances since the 2023 Fifth NCA make new syntheses particularly valuable for future national, sub-national, and sectoral climate assessments. It also identifies critical research topics in those select areas that would be useful for future climate assessment efforts. Overall, this research priorities roadmap aims to catalyze collaborations, research, and a network of climate assessments to synthesize the state of climate impacts, risks, and responses and to provide widely accessible and foundational information for sectoral, regional, and cross-cutting climate action plans and decisions in the U.S.
